articles.title: Soldados salvadorenhos morrem em explosão durante missão no Haiti | G1
articles.standfirst: Em outubro, o presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, enviou 2 mil soldados ao Haiti para combater gangues armadas.
articles.summary: Soldados salvadorenhos morrem em explosão no Haiti durante missão enviada por Nayib Bukele para combater gangues; outros dois militares ficaram feridos no acidente.
articles.body:
Dois soldados salvadorenhos morreram e outros dois ficaram feridos em uma explosão enquanto trabalhavam com material explosivo durante uma missão no Haiti, informou o Exército de El Salvador nesta sexta-feira (20).

Os militares não informaram onde ocorreu a explosão nem que tipo de explosivos estavam manuseando. Um porta-voz do governo salvadorenho afirmou que não poderia fornecer mais informações naquele momento.

No mês passado, o presidente Nayib Bukele enviou mais de 2 mil soldados ao Haiti para combater gangues armadas, depois que quatro integrantes de uma missão apoiada pela ONU desapareceram em 18 de outubro.

Bukele publicou vários vídeos de ataques a residências de líderes de gangues . Milhares de haitianos também foram às ruas em manifestações de apoio à intervenção. Analistas, porém, alertam que, sem um plano de longo prazo para garantir o controle territorial, os ataques podem acabar tendo efeitos contrários e colocando civis em risco.

(Edição de Daina Beth Solomon e Kylie Madry)

articles.title: Bicho-preguiça resgatado com filhote nas costas volta à natureza | G1
articles.standfirst: A fêmea foi encontrada ferida e em risco de atropelamento às margens de uma rodovia em Pedro de Toledo (SP). O filhote não sobreviveu.
articles.summary: A fêmea foi encontrada ferida e em risco de atropelamento às margens de uma rodovia em Pedro de Toledo (SP). O filhote não sobreviveu.
articles.body:
Bicho-preguiça resgatado com filhote nas costas em Pedro de Toledo (SP) é devolvido à natureza em Peruíbe (SP) — Foto: Divulgação/CNL

Uma fêmea de bicho-preguiça, resgatada há um mês com um filhote nas costas em uma rodovia de Pedro de Toledo (SP) , foi devolvido à natureza. A soltura aconteceu em Peruíbe (SP), após o animal se recuperar de ferimentos nas garras e escoriações nas patas. O bebê não sobreviveu.

O resgate aconteceu às margens da Rodovia Padre Manoel da Nóbrega (SP-055), no dia 12 de outubro, feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. Segundo a Concessionária Novo Litoral (CNL), os animais foram encontrados por uma equipe de inspeção de tráfego durante o monitoramento da via.

Ainda segundo a concessionária, a fêmea estava em uma situação de risco de atropelamento. A equipe acionou o apoio operacional para retirar os animais do local e encaminhá-los ao Instituto Ambiecco, instituição parceira da CNL responsável pela reabilitação de animais silvestres.

Durante o atendimento veterinário, foram identificados ferimentos nas garras e escoriações nas patas da mãe, enquanto o filhote estava debilitado e teve a morte constatada.

Após um mês de recuperação, os profissionais constataram que a fêmea estava apta para retornar ao habitat natural. A soltura, realizada na quinta-feira (19), foi acompanhada por técnicos da área de Meio Ambiente da CNL e pela equipe do Instituto Ambiecco.

Bicho-preguiça foi encontrado às margens da Rodovia Padre Manoel da Nóbrega. — Foto: Divulgação/CNL

O que fazer ao avistar um animal silvestre?

Ao avistar um animal silvestre próximo à pista ou em situação de risco, os motoristas podem entrar em contato com a CNL pelo telefone 0800-098-88-55 para solicitar atendimento.

A orientação é não tentar capturar, tocar ou transportar o animal por conta própria, pois a aproximação pode colocar em risco tanto a pessoa quanto o próprio bicho.

articles.title: TikTok lança ferramentas para identificar conteúdos de IA e deepfakes; veja como funcionam | G1
articles.standfirst: Recursos buscam combater conteúdos enganosos antes das eleições de 2027 em países europeus. Uma das ferramentas, que ainda não tem previsão de chegada ao Brasil, será voltada a figuras públicas.
articles.summary: Recursos buscam combater conteúdos enganosos antes das eleições na Europa. Uma das ferramentas, que ainda não tem previsão de chegar ao Brasil, será voltada a figuras públicas.
articles.body:
O TikTok anunciou nesta sexta-feira (20) duas novas ferramentas para identificar conteúdos criados ou manipulados por inteligência artificial (IA).

As medidas buscam ampliar a transparência sobre o uso da tecnologia e facilitar a identificação de deepfakes, como são conhecidos os vídeos, imagens e áudios manipulados por IA para simular situações reais.

Uma das novidades permitirá que qualquer pessoa verifique se uma imagem ou vídeo foi produzido ou editado com ferramentas de inteligência artificial do próprio TikTok , mesmo sem ter uma conta na rede social.

A outra, chamada Likeness Detection (detecção de semelhança), será voltada a criadores de conteúdo e figuras públicas, incluindo políticos. O recurso permitirá localizar e denunciar publicações que reproduzam sua aparência por meio de inteligência artificial, possivelmente sem consentimento.

Segundo a empresa, a primeira ferramenta já está disponível, enquanto a segunda começou a ser liberada gradualmente em diferentes países.

Os anúncios foram apresentados durante um evento sobre segurança e inovação promovido pelo TikTok em Londres, no Reino Unido.

A iniciativa também faz parte dos esforços da plataforma para combater conteúdos enganosos antes das eleições previstas para 2027 em países europeus.

Como vai funcionar a identificação de deepfakes?

A ferramenta Likeness Detection permitirá que pessoas elegíveis encontrem vídeos e contas do TikTok que possam estar utilizando sua aparência por meio de inteligência artificial.

O objetivo é facilitar a identificação de conteúdos que simulam a identidade de alguém, especialmente quando produzidos sem autorização.

Segundo a empresa, o funcionamento terá três etapas:

Verificação de identidade: o usuário deverá se cadastrar na ferramenta e confirmar sua identidade por meio de um parceiro externo de confiança.

Identificação de conteúdos: depois do cadastro, receberá notificações quando a plataforma identificar vídeos ou contas que possam estar utilizando sua aparência. O material poderá ser analisado diretamente na ferramenta.

Denúncia: caso encontre conteúdos suspeitos, o usuário poderá denunciá-los às equipes de segurança do TikTok. As publicações que violarem as regras da plataforma serão removidas.

A empresa afirma que o sistema foi desenvolvido para reduzir a coleta de dados pessoais e preservar a privacidade dos usuários. Os documentos apresentados durante a verificação de identidade não serão armazenados pelo TikTok.

O recurso não estará disponível para todos os usuários. Segundo a plataforma, poderão utilizá-lo criadores de conteúdo e figuras públicas que atendam aos critérios de elegibilidade, incluindo contas de governos, políticos e partidos.

O TikTok não detalhou, nos comunicados, um calendário específico para a disponibilização da ferramenta no Brasil.

Como verificar se uma imagem ou vídeo foi criado por IA?

A segunda ferramenta anunciada pelo TikTok será aberta a qualquer pessoa, inclusive quem não possui uma conta na rede social.

O recurso permite verificar se uma imagem ou vídeo foi criado ou editado com as ferramentas de inteligência artificial da própria plataforma.

Para utilizar a ferramenta, o usuário poderá acessar uma página específica disponibilizada pelo TikTok e enviar a imagem ou o vídeo que deseja verificar. O sistema analisará o arquivo em busca de informações que indiquem o uso de recursos de inteligência artificial da plataforma.

Segundo a empresa, a verificação utiliza duas tecnologias:

Content Credentials: sistema que registra informações sobre a origem e o processo de criação de conteúdos digitais.

VeraDura: marca-d'água invisível desenvolvida pelo TikTok, projetada para resistir melhor a alterações e tentativas de remoção.

O TikTok explica que informações sobre a origem de um conteúdo podem desaparecer quando arquivos são baixados, compartilhados ou editados. A nova ferramenta busca facilitar essa identificação.

Segundo a empresa, a ferramenta identifica conteúdos criados ou editados com seus próprios recursos de IA, sem especificar se é capaz de reconhecer materiais produzidos por outras plataformas.

Ícone do aplicativo de compartilhamento de vídeos TikTok. — Foto: AP/Matt Slocum/Arquivo

articles.title: Construção civil busca mão de obra qualificada no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: A construção civil gerou quase 10 mil vagas formais este ano no Ceará. Setor enfrenta o desafio de encontrar profissionais qualificados para as vagas.
articles.summary: A construção civil gerou quase 10 mil vagas formais este ano no Ceará. Setor enfrenta o desafio de encontrar profissionais qualificados para as vagas.
articles.body:
A construção civil gerou quase dez mil vagas de emprego formais neste ano no Ceará, conforme dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged). O setor, no entanto, tem enfrentado o desafio de encontrar candidatos qualificados para ocupar parte dessas vagas. Em busca de mais profissionais, empresas têm firmado parcerias com instituições profissionalizantes.

É o que explica o presidente do Sindicato da Indústria da Construção Civil do Ceará (Sinduscon), Patriolino Dias de Sousa. Ele destaca que o setor está em expansão, e passou de 57 mil empregos diretos no estado em 2020 para 101 mil empregos neste ano.

"Em 2026, nós estamos tendo o melhor ano da década no mercado imobiliário. Então imagina que a gente fez diversos lançamentos, e a gente tá começando essas obras agora. Então a tendência é a gente precisar de mais mão de obra. Além disso, em todo o estado do Ceará tem diversos canteiros de obras, não só no mercado imobiliário", disse o gestor.

Presidente do Sindicato da Indústria da Construção Civil do Ceará (Sinduscon), Patriolino Dias de Sousa. — Foto: TV Verdes Mares

Em meio à crescente demanda, empresas de construção civil firmaram parceria com o Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem da Indústria (Senai) para oferecer cursos voltados para área, com objetivo de formar mais profissionais. Entre as opções estão técnico em edificações, instalação hidráulica, instalação elétrica, pedreiro em alvenaria, entre outros.

Conforme a gerente do Senai no Centro de Fortaleza, Alcilane Mot, a iniciativa é uma oportunidade para quem busca o primeiro emprego ou já está trabalhando na área, mas quer uma nova função dentro da área de construção, como carpinteiro ou ferreiro, duas ocupações com alta demanda no setor.

"Os módulos são pensados entre apropriação do conhecimento técnico especializado, mas também que ele [aluno] consiga exercitar aquilo que ele está estudando, porque é no fazer que ele vai aperfeiçoar as suas habilidades e vai conseguir sair no mercado sem nenhum tipo de dificuldade", explica Alcilane.

Setor de construção civil cresceu nos últimos anos no Ceará — Foto: Fabiane de Paula/SVM

Além das aulas em sala, os cursos também levam os alunos para aulas de campo, em obras e em contato direto com equipamentos de construção. A instituição também busca empresas parceiras para que os estudantes possam começar a trabalhar ainda enquanto estudam, de modo a conciliar teoria e prática.

Foi justamente assim que o estudante Max Souza começou a fazer o curso de técnico em edificações. Ele ingressou no Senai por meio de um edital de gratuidade, sendo o primeiro da família a estudar algo no setor de infraestrutura.

Agora, Max já está trabalhando como jovem aprendiz no setor. "A gente tem um período de teoria e depois vai pro campo, nas aulas práticas, e vai pra empresa fazer as entrevistas. Fui encaminhado para duas empresas e numa delas acabei passando", explicou.

"Lá a gente tem acesso a pessoas que já estão na área há mais tempo, engenheiros, técnico em edificações, encarregados, mestre de obras, eles tão sempre disponíveis, quando a gente pergunta eles explicam pra gente, a gente vê aquilo no dia a dia", detalha sobre a experiência de estudar e trabalhar.

No caso do Senai, os cursos da área de construção civil são oferecidos de segunda a sexta na unidade Centro, localizada na avenida Padre Ibiapina, 1280. É possível conferir a grade diretamente no site da instituição.

articles.title: Quote of the Day by Dale Carnegie, “You aren't happy or unhappy  because of what you have or who you are, but it is....."
articles.summary: Dale Carnegie is the most iconic name when it comes to self-help literature.
articles.body: Dale Carnegie is the most iconic name when it comes to self-help literature. He not just taught the world 'how to win friends and influence people but also happiness, manners, success and the art of relaxation. Much before self-help became a publishing craze, Dale Carnegie was teaching people how to overcome shyness, handle criticism, deal with difficult personalities and develop confidence. His philosophy was rooted in a simple belief: success is not merely about what a person knows, but also about how they interact with others.One of the greatest American self-help writers, Carnegie was a lecturer and pioneer of self-improvement education whose ideas helped millions of people approach relationships, communication, public speaking and personal success in an entirely different way.Dale Carnegie was born on November 24, 1888, in Maryville, Missouri, USA, into a humble farming family. Financial struggles and the realities of rural life framed his youth. His parents, James William Carnagey and Amanda Elizabeth Harbison, laboured hard to provide for the family. Education was important in the household despite their circumstances. Carnegie went to the State Teacher's College in Warrensburg, Missouri where he developed an interest in public speaking and debate. He was not born to privilege or wealth and his early years were far removed from the world of publishing, business leadership and international recognition he would eventually enter. After college he sold correspondence courses, farm products and did a variety of other jobs. He also dabbled in acting and salesmanship. These experiences brought him into contact with different kinds of people and taught him the value of persuasion, confidence and communication.His experience as a salesman was especially important. He knew that technical knowledge was not enough to succeed. It was often the ability to relate to people, to understand what motivated them, and to communicate that made the difference. Carnegie’s life changed dramatically in 1912 when he started teaching public speaking at the YMCA in New York. At the time he was looking for a steady career, but soon discovered that people were hungry to learn how to speak with confidence, how to express themselves, and how to overcome their fear of speaking to an audience.He abandoned traditional theory-laden teaching and his classes became popular. Instead, he encouraged students to talk about their own experiences, to share personal stories and to learn through doing. He believed confidence could be cultivated, not just inherited. A timid person or someone who is not at ease speaking in public, could become a good communicator with preparation, rehearsal and experience.This philosophy of teaching became the foundation of the Dale Carnegie training programs, which have grown to include leadership, communication, interpersonal relationships and professional development, in addition to public speaking. Carnegie's own life was intimately tied to the principles he preached. He was a keen observer of people and was convinced that much could be learned about human behaviour from everyday meetings. His life philosophy was simple, optimistic, self-improvement, and the importance of good relationships.He wasn't a psychologist or an academic researcher. But he depended on personal experience and conversations, biographies, historical accounts and observations of successful people. He observed the ways of powerful men and tried to determine what it was in their nature that enabled them to get along with people.Carnegie was also much interested in biographies. He believed that anyone could improve their own condition by studying the lives of successful people and learning practical lessons from them. He wrote a biography of Abraham Lincoln, Lincoln the Unknown, in 1932, which revealed his interest in leadership and character. In his personal life, he was married twice. His first wife was Lolita Baucaire; they married in 1927 and divorced in 1931. In 1944 he married Dorothy Price Vanderpool who was instrumental in building and growing his training organization. They had a daughter named Donna. Carnegie became a famous public figure but his professional philosophy remained focused on everyday circumstances: how to talk to a colleague, how to deal with criticism, how to make someone feel valued, and how to stop worrying taking over your daily life.Books that transformed the self-help industryCarnegie's most important contribution to literature and popular education was his books, which turned his thoughts on human relations into practical advice.His best-known book, How to Win Friends and Influence People, appeared in 1936. It explored the value of being genuinely interested in people, listening carefully, avoiding unnecessary criticism, liking people and speaking in ways that build trust. It became an international best seller. Initially published in a relatively small print run it went on to sell millions of copies, and has been translated into many languages. The main thing he taught was that people respond better to appreciation and understanding than they do to criticism and confrontation.In 1948, he published another popular book, How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. The book provided practical ways of dealing with anxiety, uncertainty, decision making and unnecessary mental stress. Carnegie didn’t rely on elaborate theories; he used stories and examples from everyday life to show how people could approach common problems in different ways.His other works included Public Speaking and Influencing Men of Business, Lincoln the Unknown and The Quick and Easy Way to Effective Speaking. Perhaps Carnegie's most lasting influence was to make communication and interpersonal skills available to the common man.Before his training programs became popular, public speaking was often seen as a specialised skill reserved for politicians, lawyers and professional speakers. Carnegie urged the average worker, the salesman, the executive and the student to develop self-confidence and to learn to express himself effectively.His courses began to include leadership, teamwork, professional relationships, customer service and personal development. He also helped to establish the idea that people skills could be taught and practised – not just a quality of naturally confident people. His organization became an international training network. Today, Dale Carnegie programs are running in dozens of countries with professional development courses in communication, leadership and workplace effectiveness.Quote of the Day“You aren't happy or unhappy because of what you have or who you are or where you are or what you are doing, it is what you think about it.” These lines from Dale Carnegie's How to Win Friends & Influence People are iconic and sum up the reason for happiness in the most potent way. Two people can have identical lives, face identical struggles and have identical advantages, and still experience the world in a completely different way. We can always feel discontent, focusing on what we don’t have, what went wrong, or what others seem to have. The other is content with small victories, meaningful relationships and the opportunities that each day brings.Carnegie’s message is not that money, success, relationships, or life circumstances are not important. Instead he reminds us happiness is not measured by how much we have or how much we achieve. It is also shaped by what we make of our experiences. We may spend years chasing a better job, a bigger house, more recognition or a more comfortable life, thinking that happiness is just beyond the next milestone. But when we arrive, our expectations tend to leap ahead even further.But the real change, Carnegie tells us, comes when we change our perspective on life. articles.title: Watch: Woman employee confronts, thrashes executive engineer inside office over sexual harassment in UP
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A woman employee of the electricity department allegedly thrashed an executive engineer inside his office chamber in Hamirpur on Friday after
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A woman employee of the electricity department allegedly thrashed an executive engineer inside his office chamber in Hamirpur on Friday after accusing him of sexually harassing her and making inappropriate advances.The woman, a widow, alleged that, the executive engineer posted in the electricity testing division, would repeatedly call her to his cabin, make inappropriate remarks and attempt to touch her.The incident was captured on video, which surfaced on social media, showing the woman confronting and slapping the officer inside his chamber, while other employees also joined in, questioning him over the alleged misconduct.According to the woman’s allegations had been making her uncomfortable for some time by staring at her inappropriately, calling her to his chamber without any work-related reason and making personal remarks. She alleged that he had also asked her for the address of her rented accommodation over the phone.Recounting Friday's incident, she said the executive engineer called her to his chamber and asked when she would invite him home for tea. She told him that if he wanted tea, she could arrange it at the office, but she would not invite him to her residence. She alleged that he then grabbed her hand and pulled her towards him, prompting her to lose her temper and beat him.The woman further alleged that the engineer would make inappropriate remarks about her, including comments about the lines on her palm and whether someone would support her. She said she had earlier shared her concerns with colleagues, who accompanied her to the executive engineer's chamber after the incident and confronted him over his alleged behaviour.The woman also alleged that she was being pressured to reach a compromise and was receiving repeated calls from another assistant engineer. Expressing fear for her safety, she urged the police to take action and provide protection, claiming she was worried that the accused could enter her rented accommodation and harm her.The executive engineer, however, denied the allegations, claiming that he had done nothing wrong and that the woman assaulted him when he asked her to carry out official work. He also alleged that she recorded a video of him while beating him.SP, Hamirpur, Mrigank Shekhar Pathak, said the woman had submitted a written complaint and a team was sent to the spot. articles.title: Rajasthan panchayat election results 2026: 5 takeaways as Congress beats BJP; RLP makes big gains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress has turned the tables on the BJP in Rajasthan's rural local body elections, securing a decisive lead in Panchayat Samiti and Zila
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress has turned the tables on the BJP in Rajasthan's rural local body elections, securing a decisive lead in Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad polls just months after the ruling party swept the state's urban civic elections.According to State Election Commission figures reported by ANI, the Congress has won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 1,795, while in Zila Parishads, it has secured 143 seats against the BJP's 83. The figures are for declared results.The elections have also seen former BJP ally Hanuman Beniwal's Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) make significant inroads, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats. Independents have secured 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, emerging as key players in several local bodies.The results come after the BJP won boards in 197 of Rajasthan's 301 urban local bodies and could signal a shift in the state's rural political landscape.Here are five key takeaways from the results.1. Congress reverses 2020-21 rural poll trendThe Congress has emerged well ahead of the BJP in the rural polls, reversing the trend seen in the 2020-21 Panchayati Raj elections, when the BJP held the upper hand.In the main December 2020 round across 21 districts, the BJP won 353 of 636 Zila Parishad seats against the Congress's 252. It also secured control of 14-15 district boards, while the Congress won five.The BJP had also edged ahead in Panchayat Samiti elections, winning 1,989 seats against the Congress's 1,852. While the Congress recovered ground in subsequent phases, including in Jaipur, the latest results mark a substantial improvement in its rural electoral fortunes.The comparison, however, comes with a caveat. Rajasthan's administrative reorganisation has expanded the rural governance map from 33 to 41 Zila Parishads and from 352 to 457 Panchayat Samitis, making direct comparisons with previous elections difficult.Rahul Gandhi took to X to thank the people of Rajasthan. "This response has come from a state where the BJP has its own government—a direct response to the double engine," he wrote."It’s a Congress wave in Rajasthan! Bucking the trend of supporting the ruling party at the State level, the people of Rajasthan have delivered a strong verdict in the local body elections - against the BJP's complete misgovernance in Rajasthan and the Centre," said Congress Lok Sabha MP KC Venugopal."All over India, the anger against BJP is coming to the fore - first seen in July, then against Gyanesh Kumar and now with such statewide rejection of the BJP," he added.2. BJP takes hits on turf of its own leadersThe BJP's setbacks in areas associated with prominent party leaders have added to the significance of its rural poll performance.In Sikar, Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra's wife Shanti Devi and son Ajay Singh lost their Panchayat Samiti elections. His other son, Durga Singh, who contested as an Independent, was also defeated.In Jhotwara, represented by minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, the BJP reportedly won just one of the 15 seats, pointing to a difficult electoral showing in the constituency.The results, however, offered contrasting fortunes for the Congress. State party chief Govind Singh Dotasra performed strongly in his home turf of Sikar, while Tonk, associated with Sachin Pilot, also emerged as an important pocket for the party.The state BJP chief took responsibility for the loss. "Today, the election results for various Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis across Rajasthan have been announced. We accept the public mandate. We will also review where we may have faltered; we will examine these aspects and remain, as always, deeply committed to public service," Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore said.3. Former BJP ally RLP makes big gainsThe Rashtriya Loktantrik Party has emerged as one of the biggest gainers outside the two main parties, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats.The performance marks a significant expansion from the 2020 rural elections, when the RLP, then allied with the BJP, won 60 Panchayat Samiti seats and 10 Zila Parishad seats in the main round.Party chief Hanuman Beniwal has claimed that the RLP has received more votes than the BJP in Nagaur and is poised to secure the Zila Pramukh post there.He has also pointed to encouraging results in Didwana-Kuchaman, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu and parts of Jaipur, while claiming the party was heading towards a majority in Sanganer Panchayat Samiti, in Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's assembly constituency.The results reinforce the RLP's regional presence and give Beniwal greater leverage in Rajasthan's rural political landscape, particularly among its youth and farming communities.4. Congress claims JaipurThe Congress has won 14 of the 22 Panchayat Samitis in Jaipur district, emerging as the dominant party in the rural local body elections.The BJP secured majorities in Chomu and Sambhar, while the RLP won Sanganer. Five Panchayat Samitis returned fractured verdicts, potentially setting the stage for negotiations.The results have also produced contrasting outcomes for political families. Senior BJP leader Rajendra Rathore's son Parakram Singh won Zila Parishad Ward 39 by 17,861 votes, while his daughter-in-law Kanika Singh secured Ward 23 by 2,384 votes.While the Rathore family registered victories, the losses involving Jhabar Singh Kharra's family underscored that political influence did not necessarily translate into electoral success.5. Independents and smaller parties could decide rural powerThe strong showing by Independents and regional parties could prove crucial in local bodies where no party has secured a clear majority.Independents have won 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, followed by the RLP with 438. The Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) has secured 215 seats, CPI(M) 50, BSP 44 and AAP two.In Zila Parishads, Independents have won five seats, the RLP four, CPM three and BSP one.With the posts of Pradhans and Zila Pramukhs elected indirectly by ward members, the results could trigger political negotiations and alliances in several districts.Elections for Zila Pramukhs are scheduled for November 25, while Panchayat Samiti Pradhan elections will take place on November 27. Counting in Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar has been deferred to December 17.The results give the Congress a significant rural boost ahead of the 2028 assembly elections, put the BJP's grassroots connect under scrutiny and strengthen regional players such as the RLP. However, local body elections are shaped by candidate-level factors, caste equations and local issues, and are not necessarily a direct predictor of assembly electoral outcomes.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia's war spills into Poland as missile crashes near Ukraine border; PM Tusk suspects provocation
articles.summary: Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk on Friday said the crash of a Russian cruise missile in the country's southeast was likely a deliberate provocation.
articles.body: Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk on Friday said the crash of a Russian cruise missile in the country's southeast was likely a deliberate provocation. He specifically pointed to its proximity to a major military exercise involving Western allies preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.Polish defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile struck a rural area near Nowy Lipowiec, about 50 km from the Ukrainian border, at around 6.30 am. Two other objects also reportedly violated Polish airspace: another suspected missile came down near Rudnik nad Sanem, while a jet-powered drone crashed near Mołodycz.No casualties or damage were reported in Poland. The incident prompted an investigation, with military helicopters and rescue vehicles deployed near the suspected crash sites and police setting up temporary roadblocks. Schools in the vicinity of Nowy Lipowiec also suspended classes for the day, Polish news agency PAP reported.Tusk said the timing and location of the incident raised questions about whether it was accidental. The crash site was around 75 km from where thousands of European troops were participating in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland.The UK- and France-led exercise, called Koalicja 2026, involves 11 countries from the West's Coalition of the Willing. It is aimed at preparing for a possible peace deal in Ukraine and a subsequent mission to help stabilise the country and rebuild its military."It is no coincidence that these objects landed near the site where military manoeuvres by a 'coalition of the willing' supported by Polish troops are taking place in Nowa Dęba," Tusk said.Kosiniak-Kamysz described the airspace violations as a Russian provocation and said he would seek additional support from Nato.Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte said he had spoken to Tusk about the airspace violations and confirmed that NATO jets had been scrambled in response. He condemned Russia's attacks and said the alliance stood in solidarity with Poland, adding that NATO would continue to strengthen its ability to deter and defend against threats.US president Donald Trump, speaking to Fox News, said Putin had "accidentally landed a few drones and little missiles" in Poland.The incident came as Russia carried out one of its biggest aerial assaults on Ukraine since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022. Russian missiles and drones killed at least eight people and damaged infrastructure, including bridges across the Dnipro river and a railway station in Lviv, according to Ukrainian officials.The airspace violations also followed a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin, where 40 countries pledged continued support for Kyiv. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said peace talks with Russia should take place soon on neutral territory.Russia has not commented on the reported violations. The war has spilled over into neighbouring Poland before, with a cruise missile also landing in the country in July.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pahalgam attack: Beijing yet to share info on how GoPro camera US supplied to China was found on terrorists
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: China is yet to respond to India's request for information on a US-made GoPro camera recovered from the terrorists involved in the 2025
articles.body: NEW DELHI: China is yet to respond to India's request for information on a US-made GoPro camera recovered from the terrorists involved in the 2025 Pahalgam massacre, NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal said on Friday. He added that investigators had gathered some forensic evidence in the case."We have not received any reply so far… But we have some forensic evidence," Aggarwal told reporters when asked whether Beijing had responded to the agency's communication about the device.The camera has become a key lead in the NIA's efforts to trace the cross-border supply networks that provide equipment to Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). During the investigation, the agency approached US manufacturer GoPro Inc to establish the device's sales history. The company informed investigators that the camera had originally been shipped to an authorised commercial distributor in China, officials said.Investigators are now trying to establish how it moved from the Chinese distributor into the hands of LeT operatives. Officials are examining the possibility that the devices were procured by the Pakistan Army and subsequently supplied to terrorist groups, although this remains under investigation.India does not have a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) with China, meaning requests for information in such cases are pursued through diplomatic channels.The camera was recovered from the terrorists killed in an encounter in the Dachigam forests in July 2025, months after the attack on tourists in Pahalgam's Baisaran meadows. Investigators believe terrorist groups in Jammu and Kashmir have increasingly used body-worn and tactical cameras to record attacks for propaganda and psychological warfare.Chinese-origin weapons also under investigationThe camera is not the only piece of equipment that has drawn investigators' attention to China. Officials said at least two AK-47 rifles recovered from the Baisaran attack site and another recovered from the Dachigam encounter site were also of Chinese origin.The three terrorists involved in the massacre are believed to have escaped through the Pahalgam jungles after the attack on April 22, 2025, possibly using a vehicle. Investigators believe they had a window of nearly 40 minutes before security forces could fully assess the scale of the attack.A vehicle bearing a Shopian registration number was spotted on a road leading out of Pahalgam, but investigators lost track of it after finding that several CCTV cameras along the route were not functioning.The NIA has filed a chargesheet against LeT and six individuals, including the three slain terrorists – Faisal Jatt alias Suleman, Habeeb Tahir alias Chottu and Hamza Afghani – as well as the outfit's self-styled commander Sajid Jatt alias Sajid Jutt. Two local residents, Bashir Ahmad Jothatd and Parvaiz Ahmad, were also named for allegedly providing food and shelter to the terrorists before the attack.Two local residents, Bashir Ahmad Jothatd and Parvaiz Ahmad, have also been named for allegedly providing food and shelter to the terrorists in the days before the attack. Investigators said the men had supplied them with provisions, including turmeric, red chillies and salt, as well as cooking utensils, blankets and a tarpaulin.A blanket recovered from the Dachigam encounter site was traced to Bashir's home, officials said. A hair strand found on it was matched through DNA testing to the blanket taken from his house on April 21, 2025.On April 22, 2025, terrorists killed 26 people, mostly tourists, in the Baisaran meadows of Pahalgam. The massacre prompted India to launch Operation Sindoor, targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan-controlled territories, including camps belonging to the banned LeT and Jaish-e-Mohammed.The three attackers were later killed by Army special forces in an encounter in the Dachigam forests on the outskirts of Srinagar.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Colleen Begg came to Mozambique in 2002 to study honey badgers and stayed to protect one of Africa’s largest lion populations, and she is the first woman to win Prince William’s Tusk lifetime award
articles.summary: What began as a research trip to study honey badgers in Mozambique has turned into a conservation career spanning more than two decades for Dr Colleen
articles.body: What began as a research trip to study honey badgers in Mozambique has turned into a conservation career spanning more than two decades for Dr Colleen Begg. The South African conservationist, who arrived in the country in 2002, has now received one of Africa’s most significant conservation honours, recognising her efforts to protect threatened wildlife while building lasting partnerships with local communities. Begg received the 2026 Prince William Award for Conservation in Africa at the Tusk Conservation Awards in London on November 11. Prince William, the Prince of Wales and royal patron of the British conservation charity Tusk, presented the award at a ceremony held at Raffles London at The OWO. According to Tusk, Begg is the first woman to receive the lifetime achievement honour since the awards were established in 2013. The recognition was also reported by the Wildlife Conservation Network and Ninety One, the award’s supporting partner.The award acknowledges more than 30 years of Begg’s work in conservation, including over 20 years spent protecting wildlife in Mozambique’s Niassa Special Reserve. Her journey there, however, began with a very different research interest.In 2002, Begg travelled to Niassa to study honey badgers, honeyguide birds and traditional honey-gathering practices. Her research eventually brought her attention to a significant gap in scientific knowledge about the reserve’s large carnivores. Alongside her husband, fellow conservationist Keith Begg, she undertook a survey of the region’s predators. The findings laid the groundwork for the Niassa Carnivore Project, which the couple established in 2003.Today, the project works to protect lions, leopards, spotted hyenas and African wild dogs across the Niassa Special Reserve, an approximately 42,000-square-kilometre protected landscape in northern Mozambique. The reserve is home to one of Africa’s important remaining lion populations and provides a crucial habitat for other threatened carnivores.But the project’s work extends well beyond wildlife monitoring. A central part of Begg’s approach has been to address the challenges faced by people living alongside dangerous animals. Through community wildlife guardian programmes, environmental education, alternative livelihood initiatives and conflict-prevention measures, the organisation aims to make conservation beneficial to the people who share their land with wildlife.One of its notable initiatives involves restoring traditional raised homes, known locally as sanja houses. The structures elevate families above ground level, helping reduce dangerous encounters with wildlife. The project has also built a largely Mozambican workforce, with local residents playing an increasingly important role in conservation and decision-making.Begg’s commitment to the region was also tested by a deadly security incident. In April 2025, insurgents attacked the Mariri Environmental Centre and the Niassa Carnivore Project’s headquarters, killing four anti-poaching scouts. The attack severely disrupted conservation activities and affected families connected to the project.However, Begg and her team returned to support those affected, continue essential programmes and rebuild damaged infrastructure. Tusk recognised this resilience as an important part of her contribution, alongside her efforts to develop a conservation organisation that can eventually be led entirely by Mozambicans.Her influence also reaches beyond Mozambique. In 2017, Begg co-founded Women for the Environment Africa (WE Africa), an initiative that supports and connects women working in environmental conservation across the continent. The organisation aims to strengthen women’s leadership and ensure they have a greater role in shaping conservation policies and decisions.Begg was among three conservationists recognised at this year’s Tusk ceremony. Kenyan conservationist Raabia Hawa, founder of the Ulinzi Africa Foundation, received the Tusk Award for Conservation in Africa for her work addressing wildlife crime. Daniel Yiankere, security manager at Kenya’s Loisaba Conservancy, received the Tusk Wildlife Ranger Award in recognition of his decades of service protecting wildlife.For Begg, the lifetime achievement honour represents more than an individual milestone. It also brings international attention to the people of Niassa, the Mozambican conservation teams and the community partnerships that have sustained the project for more than 20 years. Her work has increasingly focused on ensuring that the next generation of local conservationists has the skills, opportunities and leadership roles needed to carry it forward.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2017, an artist placed 48 figures in a circle off Indonesia to highlight coral-reef loss; within a year, soft corals and sponges had colonized them
articles.summary: Discover how British artist Jason deCaires Taylor's underwater sculpture installation, Nest, off the coast of Gili Meno, Indonesia, is transforming marine habitats and raising awareness about coral reef loss.
articles.body: Beneath the ocean’s surface, human figures stand where marine life would typically thrive. Their very existence broaches an unusual question: can artwork become part of the ecosystem it occupies?According to Underwater Sculpture’s report in 2017, 48 human figures were placed four metres beneath the waters of Gili Meno, an Indonesian island between Bali and Lombok. Arranged in a circle on the seabed, the sculptures formed Nest, an underwater installation by British artist Jason deCaires Taylor. The work was designed to provide a surface for marine organisms to settle, bearing in mind the eventual formation of a reef intended to give the installation an ecological function beyond its aesthetic appeal. Taylor’s project merged both sculpture and marine habitat creation. Each figure was life-size, including embracing couples curled up on the seabed.An art gallery in shallow watersThe installation sat about four metres below the surface, making it accessible to snorkellers. Gili Meno is one of the three islands in the Gili group, situated between Bali and Lombok. Its clear waters and turtle population are among the natural features identified in the project’s description.According to a Wandering Educators report in 2017, after the final figures had been installed, they were opened to the public. The work was one of Taylor’s most ambitious installations and his first project in the Asian region, the outlet reported.Before he made Nest, Taylor had spent more than a decade creating underwater installations in locations including the Caribbean, the Canary Islands and the River Thames. His earlier projects included Museo Atlántico in Lanzarote and the Museo Subacuático de Arte in Mexico, as reported by Wandering Educators.Sustainable by design The figures were made using pH-neutral, environmental-grade concrete, while other materials included stainless steel, basalt and aggregates. The concrete was selected to provide a suitable surface for marine organisms such as corals, sponges and filter-feeding organisms.The plans of BASK Gili Meno, the resort developer, also shaped the context for the sculptures. The resort was planned to comprise villas featuring energy-saving technology, sustainable materials and architecture intended to respect the island’s natural surroundings and local culture, Wandering Educators reported, sustainable materials and architecture intended to respect the island’s natural surroundings and local culture, Wandering Educators reported.Turning underwater art into ocean awareness The project was conceived against a backdrop of declining coral populations. According to Wandering Educators, about 40% of the world’s coral reefs had been lost over the preceding decades, and scientists had warned that further losses were likely to occur. Taylor intended the installation to evoke a sense of awareness in visitors about what lay beneath the water and the vulnerability of marine habitats. For Taylor, the sculptures represented a connection between people and the natural environment. In an interview with Wandering Educators in 2017, he said: “First and foremost, Nest is an environmental space.But Nest is also a bridge between the human and marine worlds.”The installation was commissioned by BASK Gili Meno. Its position within swimming distance of a publicly accessible beach meant that visitors could observe the figures underwater. Visitors did not need access to a restricted resort facility.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Blink-182's Mark Hoppus won a legal battle over a neighbour's trees blocking his Beverly Hills view, but says she still owes nearly $681,000 in legal fees and interest; he is now trying to collect
articles.summary: Blink-182 bassist Mark Hoppus has won a lengthy legal battle against his Beverly Hills neighbour over a row of pine trees that blocked his view of the
articles.body: Blink-182 bassist Mark Hoppus has won a lengthy legal battle against his Beverly Hills neighbour over a row of pine trees that blocked his view of the city. However, the musician is now trying to recover nearly $681,000 in unpaid legal fees and interest linked to the case. Court documents filed by Hoppus's legal team on 16 November 2026 in Los Angeles County Superior Court state that the defendant, Anastasia DeSimone, has not paid the amount ordered by the court. Hoppus first filed the lawsuit in 2024, claiming that mature pine trees on DeSimone's neighbouring property had grown too tall and violated local rules and private agreements designed to protect views in the Trousdale Estates area. The dispute was reported by the Los Angeles Times.According to court filings, Hoppus argued that the trees had seriously affected his ability to enjoy and use his home. He asked the court to order DeSimone to trim or remove them. Although the exact terms of the original settlement were not made public in the initial reports, recent court filings show that Hoppus won the case and was awarded legal costs. He is now asking the court to enforce payment of $664,606 in legal fees and another $16,231 in accumulated interest, bringing the total to $680,837. His legal team has indicated that it will use all available legal options to recover the money if efforts to reach a settlement fail.Background of the neighbourhood disputeThe dispute reflects a common problem in wealthy hillside neighbourhoods, where the value of a property can depend heavily on its views. Arguments over tree heights, landscaping and blocked views are not unusual in these areas. Such disagreements can end up in court when neighbours fail to reach an agreement through direct discussions or mediation. The Los Angeles Times reported that Hoppus had bought his property as a major investment, with the expectation that it would offer an open view of the surrounding city.His lawsuit claimed that DeSimone had failed to keep the trees at the agreed height, creating a nuisance and affecting his property rights. In hillside communities such as Trousdale Estates, homeowners may be subject to specific rules known as covenants, conditions and restrictions (CC&Rs). These rules, along with local regulations, can set limits on vegetation and tree heights to protect views shared by residents. Hoppus's lawyers argued that the rules were being breached and that court action was needed to protect his right to enjoy the view from his property. The dispute centred on whether the trees had been maintained according to the standards agreed upon by the neighbouring property owners.Legal costs and enforcement proceedingsCourts can order one party to pay the other side's legal expenses in civil cases, particularly when an individual has to take legal action to protect rights or enforce an agreement. In Hoppus's case, the $664,606 in legal fees reflects the cost of a dispute that lasted around two years, from the original lawsuit in 2024 to the latest enforcement action in late 2026. After the court ruled in Hoppus's favour, DeSimone became responsible for paying the awarded legal costs. However, the latest court filing indicates that the amount remains unpaid. Hoppus's legal team has now filed a writ of execution, a formal legal order that allows officials to take steps to recover money owed under a court judgment. This can allow law enforcement authorities, including the sheriff, to seize certain assets belonging to the person who owes the money. Depending on the circumstances and the court's order, these assets may include money held in bank accounts, property or income. The recovered funds can then be used to pay the outstanding judgment.The filing suggests that the deadline for DeSimone to make the payment has passed without the amount being settled. Hoppus is therefore seeking to use the legal process to recover the money rather than relying only on further discussions between the parties. The latest development also shows that winning a lawsuit does not always mean the financial dispute is over. Although Hoppus has secured a favourable court decision and an award covering his legal expenses, he still has to complete the process of collecting the money. The case also highlights the potentially high costs of property disputes involving blocked views, particularly in wealthy neighbourhoods where homeowners may rely on private agreements and local rules to protect the appearance and value of their properties. Neither Mark Hoppus nor Anastasia DeSimone has publicly commented on the latest court filing or the attempt to recover the outstanding $680,837.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: At least 36 Southern California trains burglarised in $22.5 million cargo theft racket; 14 accused allegedly stole Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools, sold goods on black market for over $1 million
articles.summary: In a major cargo theft case in the United States, 14 people have been indicted for allegedly stealing more than $22.5 million worth of goods, including
articles.body: In a major cargo theft case in the United States, 14 people have been indicted for allegedly stealing more than $22.5 million worth of goods, including Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools, from freight trains in Southern California. The accused allegedly targeted high-value cargo trains, forced them to make emergency stops and stole products that were later sold on the black market. Investigators have also alleged that the group used Instagram to coordinate their activities and connect with potential buyers.According to a statement released by the US Department of Justice (DOJ), the alleged gang carried out burglaries on at least three dozen freight trains between February 2024 and August 2026. Thirteen of the 14 accused were arrested on Thursday, while the case has been filed under a 17-count federal indictment.First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli described the scale of the alleged operation as staggering. "We have charged a crew of 14 in a scheme to steal more than $22.5 million in cargo from at least three dozen freight trains in Southern California," he said. He also warned that authorities would pursue not only those allegedly stealing the goods but also those knowingly making money by reselling stolen cargo.How the gang allegedly targeted freight trainsAccording to investigators, the operation was led by 21-year-old Nathan Daniel Angel of East Los Angeles. The indictment alleges that he identified high-value freight trains carrying Nike sneakers and other products arriving through the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.The group allegedly had a planned method of stopping the trains. Some members would identify locations along the railway tracks, while others allegedly cut the trains' air hoses, forcing them to make emergency stops. Once the trains halted, members would board them and remove valuable cargo.Other accused individuals allegedly arranged trucks and vans to transport the stolen goods. They also reportedly acted as lookouts and helped move the products to storage locations, including private residences.The alleged thefts took place along railway tracks in Pico Rivera, Fullerton and other locations across Southern California.Nike sneakers allegedly sold to resale business for over $1 millionOne of the significant aspects of the investigation involves the alleged resale of thousands of stolen Nike sneakers. According to the indictment, Nathan Angel informed other members about the products stolen from the trains and discussed potential resale prices.He allegedly sent photographs of stolen Nike sneakers and other merchandise to several co-defendants, sometimes while the train burglaries were still taking place.Investigators have alleged that two accused individuals, Fredy Marquina and Carlos Luis Fernando Martinez, contacted potential buyers and sold stolen products to a Los Angeles-based sneaker and streetwear resale business identified in the indictment as Company 1.Between May and October 2025, the two allegedly sold thousands of pairs of stolen Nike sneakers, many still packed in their original factory cartons. The indictment states that they received approximately $1,081,493 from the business for the stolen sneakers and other merchandise.The business was allegedly not an authorised Nike reseller and went on to sell the products for a profit.Another accused individual, Jorge Angel Aguilar Espinoza, allegedly obtained stolen Nike sneakers and other goods from suppliers, including Nathan Angel. He reportedly stored the merchandise at his residence, advertised it to potential buyers through social media accounts and sold it for profit.Who are the 14 people named in the indictment?The federal indictment names 14 defendants, including members of the same family. Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, has been identified as the alleged leader of the group. His father, Daniel Angel, 38, and his uncles, Rodolfo Angel, 23, and Jose Luis Angel, 23, are also among those charged.The other defendants are Donta Hedgeman, 27; Fernando Alexis Alvarado Villegas, 27; Daniel Garcia, 36; Carlos Robert Estrada, 28; Angel Sanchez, 24; Ruben Mario Banuelos, 26; Fredy Marquina, 25; Carlos Luis Fernando Martinez, 23; Jorge Angel Aguilar Espinoza, 36; and Ricardo Mares, 32.The accused are from various neighbourhoods in and around Los Angeles, including East Los Angeles, Whittier, Commerce and South Los Angeles.What charges do they face?All 14 defendants have been charged with conspiracy. The indictment also includes 14 counts involving theft of interstate railroad cargo and possession or receipt of stolen interstate railroad cargo, along with two counts of violence against railroad carriers.If convicted, the accused could face up to five years in federal prison for the conspiracy charge and up to 10 years for each cargo theft charge. articles.title: Bridge for a bridge? Russia's tit-for-tat strategy in Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukraine struck at the heart of Russia's military supply network. Now, Moscow appears to be returning the blow by targeting Kyiv's transport lifelines.
articles.body: Ukraine struck at the heart of Russia's military supply network. Now, Moscow appears to be returning the blow by targeting Kyiv's transport lifelines.Days after Ukrainian forces damaged the strategically vital Crimean Bridge, Russia launched a massive overnight assault on Ukraine, hitting three key bridges in the capital in what could mark a dangerous escalation into a tit-for-tat war against critical infrastructure.According to the BBC, Russia targeted three major bridges in Kyiv, the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge, Darnytskyi Bridge and Southern Bridge, during a massive overnight missile and drone assault. Ballistic missiles struck the key crossings, forcing their closure to traffic and disrupting movement across the Ukrainian capital.The attack came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened retaliation for Ukraine's strike on the strategically important Crimean Bridge. Putin warned that Moscow's response would be "far more painful", signalling a possible escalation in the tit-for-tat attacks on critical infrastructure.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the latest offensive as one of the most massive strikes of the war, saying Russia had launched more than 110 missiles and over 400 attack drones across the country.According to the BBC, at least nine people were killed, including seven in Kyiv and two in Lviv. Residential buildings, energy facilities and the Sknyliv railway station in Lviv were also damaged.Kyiv's bridges are critical to the Ukrainian capital's transport network because they connect areas on either side of the Dnipro River, which divides the city into eastern and western banks.The three targeted crossings were closed following the strikes, prompting Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko to urge residents to avoid unnecessary travel by private vehicles. The disruption is significant because these bridges carry daily commuter traffic and facilitate the movement of goods and essential services across the capital.The Darnytskyi Bridge is particularly important as it carries both road and railway traffic. The Southern Bridge serves as a major crossing in southern Kyiv, while the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge connects the Podil district with the eastern side of the city.Their disruption could complicate civilian movement, emergency response and the transportation of essential supplies. From a military perspective, bridges are also potential logistical chokepoints, making them strategically important during a prolonged conflict.Russia's tit-for-tat strategyThe latest strikes highlight an escalating cycle of attacks on critical infrastructure by both sides. Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the Crimean Bridge, first in October 2022 with a truck bombing and again in July 2023 using sea drones.In its latest operation, Kyiv targeted the bridge after reportedly weakening Russian air-defence systems protecting it. The crossing is a key supply route for Moscow, connecting mainland Russia with occupied Crimea and facilitating the movement of military equipment, fuel and personnel.Ukraine's broader strategy has focused on disrupting Russian military logistics by striking fuel infrastructure, railway networks, oil facilities and transport routes in occupied territories.Russia, meanwhile, has repeatedly targeted Ukraine's energy facilities, railway networks and transport infrastructure to disrupt civilian movement and military supplies. The latest assault on three Kyiv bridges, alongside strikes on railway and energy infrastructure, fits into this wider campaign.The two sides are increasingly using infrastructure strikes to impose logistical and economic costs on each other. While Ukraine is attempting to weaken Russia's supply lines to occupied territories, Moscow is putting pressure on Ukraine's transport connectivity and essential services.Putin's warning that Russia's response to the Crimean Bridge attack would be "far more painful" adds to the perception of a tit-for-tat escalation, although the Kremlin has not explicitly confirmed the Kyiv strikes were retaliation for that operation.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday hailed the party's performance in Rajasthan's panchayat elections, taking a swipe at the BJP saying the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday hailed the party's performance in Rajasthan's panchayat elections, taking a swipe at the BJP saying the results reflected "the voice of every village" in the country.Sharing a post on X, Rahul thanked voters in rural Rajasthan for placing their trust in Congress, saying the mandate had become the party's responsibility."Heartfelt thanks to our brothers and sisters in rural Rajasthan. The trust you have placed in Congress in the panchayat elections is now our responsibility," he said.Rahul alleged that the results were a direct response to the BJP's "double engine" government, accusing the ruling party of weakening MGNREGA, hurting farmers and stripping panchayats of their powers."The BJP attacked MGNREGA, pushed farmers into losses, and stripped panchayats of their powers. Inflation, unemployment, and migration have emptied the villages," he said."The villages were watching everything, enduring everything. Now they have spoken. This is not just Rajasthan's mandate, it is the voice of every village in the country," Rahul added.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the party's victory in the Panchayati Raj elections showed that people were determined to hold the BJP accountable for its "double-engine misrule"."From Rajasthan to other states across the country, people are looking to Congress with hope and trust. Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan. Warm congratulations to all the dedicated leaders and hardworking workers of @INCRajasthan, who came together to raise grassroots issues and strengthen the people's trust," he said in a Hindi post on X.Kharge said the trust placed in the party by voters was its greatest responsibility.Meanwhile, the BJP state president accepted defeat and said that party respected the people's mandate and would introspect on its performance following the results."Today, the election results for various Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis across Rajasthan have been announced. We accept the public mandate" Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore said.“We will also review where we may have faltered; we will examine these aspects and remain, as always, deeply committed to public service," he added.The results come as a setback to the BJP ahead of the Bhajanlal Sharma-led government's third anniversary in December, PTI reported.According to figures on the State Election Commission website on Friday evening, results were available for 7,393 of the 7,543 Panchayat Samiti seats and 981 of the 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 districts.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Don't let me suffer like this’: Texas death row inmate screams in pain during hour-long execution
articles.summary: A Texas death row inmate screamed in pain and repeatedly asked God to end his suffering during a lethal injection that took 63 minutes to complete,
articles.body: A Texas death row inmate screamed in pain and repeatedly asked God to end his suffering during a lethal injection that took 63 minutes to complete, raising fresh questions about the use of the execution drug pentobarbital in the US.Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was executed on Thursday at a penitentiary in Huntsville for the 1996 murder of diamond dealer Janos Szucs. Witnesses said Dennes moaned, groaned and complained of severe pain after the procedure began, repeatedly telling officials that something was wrong.“Don't let me suffer like this,” Dennes pleaded during the execution, according to witness accounts reported by the Associated Press. He also shouted, “My right leg is killing me!” and said, “I don't think this is normal.”The execution was completed at 7.07 pm, around 63 minutes after Dennes was strapped to the gurney. He was pronounced dead a minute later.Staff struggled to find suitable veins before injectionPrison officials acknowledged that the execution team had difficulty finding suitable veins to administer the lethal dose. Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokeswoman Amanda Hernandez said there had been several unsuccessful attempts before staff inserted the needles into Dennes's left foot and the left side of his neck.However, Hernandez maintained that the execution followed state procedures. She also questioned Dennes's complaints, saying he had reported pain before the drugs began flowing and in parts of his body where no intravenous lines had been attempted.Asked whether Dennes might have been exaggerating or faking the pain, Hernandez suggested that this could have been the case. She said complaints of pain during executions were not unprecedented.Witnesses described a prolonged and distressing procedure. The Associated Press reporter Michael Graczyk, who has witnessed numerous executions, said the delay before witnesses were allowed into the chamber was unusually long. Such delays can occur when an inmate resists or prison staff struggle to locate veins.Reverend Jeff Hood, another witness, told USA Today that Dennes's execution was “by far the worst one” he had witnessed.Failed execution attempt in Tennessee renewed scrutiny of drugDennes's execution comes amid renewed scrutiny of pentobarbital following the failed execution attempt of Christa Pike in Tennessee in September. Pike, 50, survived two doses of the drug and was taken to hospital in critical condition. Her lawyers alleged that the injections did not enter her bloodstream properly and instead pooled in her arms, leaving them burned and blistered.Pentobarbital is a powerful sedative that slows activity in the nervous system. In high doses, it is used by some US states to carry out executions through lethal injection.Its use has faced criticism over concerns that it could cause unnecessary pain and suffering. A federal review during the Biden administration raised questions about the drug, and the government subsequently prohibited its use in federal executions. The restriction, however, does not apply to individual states, which can decide their own execution methods.Dennes was convicted of murdering diamond dealer Janos Szucs, who was found shot multiple times in his Houston office in January 1996. One of the witnesses at the execution was Janice Copeland, whose husband, David, was a security guard shot during the robbery. He survived the shooting but died five years ago.Dennes's execution was the second carried out in the US on Thursday. Florida also executed 71-year-old Thomas Mitchell Overton, who was convicted of murdering a pregnant woman and her husband during a home invasion.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Meet Maddy Goldberg: Toronto chef leaves stressful fine dining career to follow her passion, cooks 100 free meals every Tuesday using random food bank ingredients to feed people in need
articles.summary: Meet Maddy Goldberg, a Toronto-based chef who is using her culinary skills to make a difference in the lives of people in need.
articles.body: Meet Maddy Goldberg, a Toronto-based chef who is using her culinary skills to make a difference in the lives of people in need. Every Tuesday, she prepares 100 free hot meals at a local food bank, using whatever ingredients are available to her. What makes her initiative special is the way she transforms ordinary groceries into creative, filling dishes, proving that good food does not always need expensive ingredients.Goldberg's journey towards community service began in 2021, when she was struggling with the pressure of working in the fine dining industry. Although she had built a career around cooking, she had once considered pursuing social work. The desire to help people, however, never really went away.How a conversation inspired her to volunteer at a food bankGoldberg recalled that after working for three years at a Toronto restaurant, her boss asked if there was anything else she wanted to explore professionally. She was offered opportunities to learn skills such as fishmongering and butchery. However, her response was rather unexpected.She expressed an interest in volunteering at a food bank. Although her employer could not arrange that opportunity, the conversation stayed with her.Eventually, Goldberg stepped away from the restaurant industry and started her own private dining business. The change gave her more flexibility and, for the first time, she had a free Tuesday."I just reached out to my local food bank, and I asked if I could volunteer," she told Good Good Good.That decision turned into a weekly commitment. Since 2021, Goldberg has volunteered at Fort York Food Bank in downtown Toronto, where she prepares lunch for people and families who need assistance.Cooking 100 meals with whatever ingredients are availableFort York Food Bank operates like a free grocery store, allowing people from low-income households to select groceries and prepare meals at home. Alongside this service, Goldberg takes responsibility for preparing around 100 hot meals every Tuesday.Her cooking process is far from conventional. Instead of planning elaborate menus and sourcing specific ingredients, she works with whatever happens to be available at the food bank. This often requires creativity, quick thinking and the ability to turn basic ingredients into something delicious.Goldberg also documents her weekly cooking sessions through Instagram Reels, sharing videos under the caption, "POV cooking lunch for 100 people using the random food I find at the food bank."Her videos have offered viewers a glimpse into how simple ingredients can be transformed into wholesome meals without spending a fortune.Red lentil fritters are among her favourite creationsIn one of her recent videos, shared on November 18, Goldberg showcased red lentil fritters made using ingredients available at the food bank.She recalled that the ingredients initially seemed rather ordinary, with onions, carrots, potatoes, eggs and milk available. However, she eventually came across a bag of raw red lentils and decided to experiment with them.She blended the lentils to prepare falafel-style fritters and served them with carrot and chickpea curry and toasted pita bread.Goldberg told Good Good Good that the dish turned out to be one of her favourite creations. She explained that the challenge was to find an unexpected way of using familiar ingredients rather than relying on conventional recipes.For instance, lentils are commonly used to prepare soups, dals and curries. Goldberg enjoys exploring different possibilities and showing people how everyday ingredients can be turned into something exciting.Why the chef believes small acts of kindness can make a differenceFor Goldberg, the initiative is about much more than cooking. She wants people to understand the value of food, reduce waste and recognise how much can be achieved with limited resources.Her decision to volunteer also came from a period when she was questioning her place in the fine dining industry. The pressure of the profession had left her thinking about larger social issues and what she could personally do to make a difference.Rather than simply discussing those concerns, she decided to take action in a way that felt meaningful to her.She told Good Good Good that she wanted to do something where the objective was not to earn money but simply to feed people. Cooking, after all, was what had drawn her to the profession in the first place.Goldberg also believes that people can contribute to society by taking small, practical steps towards causes they genuinely care about. As she put it, if everyone identified something they were passionate about and did just one thing in their everyday lives to support it, the world would be a better place.Through her weekly efforts, Goldberg is showing that making a difference does not always require a grand gesture. Sometimes, it can begin with an apron, a few everyday ingredients and 100 warm meals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: An Australian television reporter has become an unexpected social media sensation after viewers were left distracted by her muscular arms during a live
articles.body: An Australian television reporter has become an unexpected social media sensation after viewers were left distracted by her muscular arms during a live news report. A video of Seven News Sunshine Coast journalist Saavanah Bourke reporting on an emergency incident in Queensland has garnered more than 13 million views, with thousands of people commenting on her physique rather than the news she was delivering.The clip, shared on the 7NEWS Sunshine Coast Instagram account on November 17, showed Bourke reporting on a suspicious package discovered in Maroochydore, Australia. Wearing a grey asymmetrical dress that left her arms exposed, the reporter delivered an update from the scene as emergency services responded to the incident.It was her prominently defined biceps and shoulders that caught viewers' attention and the video was flooded with comments not on what Bourke was reporting, but on her biceps.One viewer joked that Bourke's arms needed an exclusion zone of their own, while another called her the strongest reporter in Australia. Several users admitted they had barely paid attention to the actual news report because they were too busy looking at her arms. Others asked about her workout routine and how she had developed such a muscular physique. Some compared their own gym memberships to donations after seeing her arms, while others praised her for challenging conventional expectations of how television journalists look.What was the news report about?Bourke was covering a suspicious package discovered at a building in Maroochydore, on Australia's Sunshine Coast in Queensland.Police, firefighters and paramedics responded to the incident, and authorities established an exclusion zone around the area as a precaution. More than 1,000 workers in the vicinity were evacuated while emergency personnel dealt with the situation.Bourke appeared in a grey outfit, holding a microphone with both hands as she delivered the update.Who is Saavanah Bourke?While her muscular appearance may have surprised viewers unfamiliar with her background, Bourke has spent years pursuing fitness alongside her journalism career. Originally from Australia's Gold Coast, she was a competitive gymnast and reportedly trained for as many as 30 hours a week before retiring from the sport.She moved towards weight training and began participating in bodybuilding competitions in 2017. Bourke is also a qualified fitness coach and runs an online coaching platform called Saavfit. Through the platform, she aims to help people develop sustainable exercise habits and find physical activities they enjoy rather than treating exercise as a chore.She regularly shares workout videos, gym updates and fitness photographs on Instagram, where she has built a following of nearly 60,000 people.Not her first viral momentThe journalist's physique had attracted attention even before the latest television clip went viral.Fitness coach Aaron Cooper previously shared a reaction video praising Bourke's muscular arms and shoulders after watching her on television. In the video, Cooper expressed surprise at her physique and suggested that she should consider working in fitness coaching. He praised her television presentation skills but joked that he would be willing to listen to her fitness advice and change his own workout routine. Bourke's mother, Linder, also joined the conversation, explaining that her daughter had trained hard for most of her life.She revealed that Bourke had spent years in competitive gymnastics, training for up to 30 hours a week, before moving on to gym workouts and other forms of exercise. Bourke has previously attributed her fitness progress to consistency and making an effort to show up for training every day.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
