articles.title: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "People think that at the end of the day a man is the only answer. Actually, a fulfilling job is…"
articles.summary: For a very long time, a woman's happiness was measured by one question. Is she married?
articles.body: For a very long time, a woman's happiness was measured by one question. Is she married? Her job, her savings and whatever she liked doing in her free time came later, and only if they didn't get in the way of her role as a wife. Princess Diana's words go against that thinking. According to her, a job that means something to you can give you what a relationship sometimes can't, a reason to get up in the morning and a feeling that you've achieved something yourself.That thought hasn't aged at all. Being in love is lovely, and most of us want it. But one person cannot be the whole source of your happiness, and work you care about can help you grow and know who you are even when you're on your own.Diana was one of the most photographed women of her time, and she paid a price for it with constant press attention and a lot of personal difficulty. Still, she put real effort into her public work. In 1987 she shook hands with an HIV patient at a London hospital without wearing gloves, at a time when many people wrongly believed the virus spread through touch. She also spent time with homeless people and others whom society had largely ignored. So when she talks about finding meaning in work, she's speaking from experience. And what she says applies to pretty much anyone who's trying to live by their own values.Quote of the day by Princess Diana"People think that at the end of the day a man is the only answer. Actually, a fulfilling job is better for me."What is the meaning of Princess Diana's quoteIn simple words, you don't need a partner to have a full and happy life.By "a man is the only answer", Diana means the old belief that a woman will only be truly happy once she's in a relationship. She doesn't agree. For her, satisfaction came from doing work that felt worthwhile.A good job does a lot more for you than pay the bills. You get responsibility. You keep learning, you use what you're good at, and at the end of the day you know you've added something. When the rest of life feels uncertain, having a goal at work can keep you going.Diana isn't saying relationships are useless, though, or that everyone should choose a career over love. She's simply questioning why romance has to be treated as the answer to everybody's happiness.A person can enjoy company and still want a life of their own. You can be happily in a relationship and not expect your partner to take care of all your emotional needs and your sense of purpose as well.When happiness comes from a few different places, it's usually more stable than when it depends on one person.Why Princess Diana's words challenged traditional expectationsIn many societies, marriage was seen for generations as the most important event in a woman's life. Women did slowly get more support for working, but the expectations around marriage and family stayed more or less where they were.That left a lot of women stuck in the middle, trying to follow their own plans while also keeping everyone else happy. If a woman picked her career, married late or spent time on herself, people often called it strange. Some called it selfish.What Diana said gave value to a woman's work and to how good it feels to do that work well.You still see this pressure today, even if no one says it out loud. Anyone who has been to an Indian wedding knows the questions. "When is your turn?" "Any good news?" "Why are you working so much, when will you settle down?"Hearing this again and again can make a person feel something is missing from their life. Diana's view is different. A good life can be made from your interests and your skills, from the things you're responsible for, and from what you do for people around you.How a fulfilling job can provide a sense of purposeWork takes up a huge part of our lives, so when it feels meaningful, it helps a lot. It gives your days a routine and a reason to keep improving.Your job doesn't have to be your dream or your passion, by the way. A steady income matters, as do reasonable hours, nice colleagues and an office that isn't toxic. A job can be fulfilling simply because it keeps you secure or because it lets you support your family. It might teach you new things, or give you enough freedom to enjoy life outside work.People find this feeling in different things. One person enjoys solving a hard problem. Another feels best when they've helped somebody, and someone else enjoys making things from scratch, teaching, looking after others or running their own business.What matters is whether the work connects with something you care about, or whether you're just passing the time till 6 pm.A teacher might feel it when a quiet child finally raises their hand. A nurse might feel it on the day a patient goes home. For an artist it could be the moment a painting finally looks right, and a journalist might feel it when readers write in to say a story helped them understand something.None of these moments has anything to do with being in a relationship, and yet they make people feel proud.Why financial independence mattersA fulfilling job usually also means earning your own money, which gives you more control over your life.With your own income you can take care of your needs and plan for later. You get to decide where you live and how. And if a relationship becomes unhealthy, or stops matching what you believe in, money of your own means you have options.This doesn't mean you have to manage everything by yourself. Partners share costs, help each other and build a life together. What financial security does is make sure nobody stays in a relationship just because they can't afford to leave.Better access to education, jobs and fair pay has given women in particular many more choices than before. It isn't only a women's issue, though. Anyone who can support themselves has more freedom to decide based on what they actually need, instead of out of fear.So when Diana talks about work, she's also talking about independence, about having the means to make your own choices.Why a relationship cannot provide every kind of fulfilmentA partner can give you love, closeness, company and support, and that can mean a great deal. But expecting one person to meet every need you have isn't fair to them or to you.We need friends too. We need hobbies, things that keep our minds busy, our own goals, and some time alone to understand ourselves. If all of your happiness depends on the relationship, then even a normal argument about something small can feel like your whole world is shaking.However supportive your partner is, they can't pick a career for you. They can't learn skills on your behalf, and they can't give you every moment of achievement in your life.Work gives you a separate part of life where you can grow and track your own progress, and it can sit quite happily alongside a relationship.This is the balance the quote is talking about. Your relationship can add a lot to your life, but it shouldn't be the only thing that makes you feel valued.The importance of building an identity beyond relationshipsProbably the most useful thing in Diana's words is the reminder to keep an identity that is your own.Everyone changes a bit in a relationship. You start watching your partner's favourite shows, you decide things together, and you take on new responsibilities. Most of that is good. The problem comes when someone slowly drops everything they used to enjoy and every plan they had for themselves.A career helps you stay yourself, and so can a creative hobby, a role in your community or some long-term goal.It matters even more when life takes a turn. Relationships sometimes end, family responsibilities change, and careers rarely go exactly as planned. At times like that, your interests, your skills and your values are still there with you.Being independent doesn't mean you never compromise, and it doesn't mean you care less about the people close to you. A healthy relationship just gives both people room to keep growing.How to apply Princess Diana's quote in daily lifeIf you've ever felt judged by whether or not you're in a relationship, these steps may help.Identify what gives you a sense of purpose. Notice when you feel completely involved in what you're doing, or useful, or proud of yourself. It might be at work. It might also be while volunteering, studying or doing something creative.Set goals that belong to you. Whether you're single, dating or married, a goal of your own gives you direction. Maybe it's learning a skill, completing a course, saving for something or handling a new project.Invest in your abilities. Improving your skills at work builds confidence and brings new opportunities. Slow progress is still progress.Build financial security where possible. When you know what you earn, what you spend and what you'll need in the future, decisions become easier to make.Maintain friendships and interests. Friends and hobbies give you support and fun that have nothing to do with your job or your love life.Question external expectations. Getting married, getting promoted and having children are personal decisions and don't come with a deadline. You're allowed to decide based on your own life and your own priorities.Make room for rest. Don't let your job become one more thing to stress about. You're worth more than what you produce, and you need time off and time with people you love, as well as time to recover.Does choosing work over romance mean rejecting loveNo. Diana is questioning the habit of depending on romance for happiness. She isn't rejecting love.Notice that she says "better for me". She's describing what makes her feel satisfied, and she isn't telling the rest of the world to put their careers first.Some people are happiest with their families. For others it's work, or helping people, or something creative, and for many it's a bit of everything. These priorities can also change over the years.Nobody has to rank these things in the same order. The point is that a relationship is one part of your life and won't automatically cure loneliness or confusion, or give you a purpose.A good relationship can actually help both people chase their goals. And a single person can have a life that's full of people, meaning and purpose.Instead of asking whether work or love is more important, it's more useful to ask whether your choices are helping you grow and live according to what you believe in.Why the quote remains relevant todayPeople still connect with this quote because the pressure to reach certain milestones by a certain age hasn't gone away. Social media makes it worse. In a few minutes of scrolling you'll see an engagement, two weddings, someone's promotion and a holiday that looks perfect, and you rarely see the bad days behind any of it.Comparing your everyday life with someone else's best moments can easily make you feel left behind. Diana's words are a reminder that a fulfilling life isn't measured by one milestone or by your relationship status.Plenty of single people are perfectly happy with their lives. Plenty of married people are deeply committed to their careers. Some find purpose in looking after family, others in running a small shop or helping their neighbourhood. Everyone's version looks different.It's also true that work isn't simple for everyone. Many people don't get to do a job they love, and financial pressure limits what they can choose. Nobody should take this quote to mean that if you don't enjoy your job, you've failed at life. Meaning can come from many places, and you can't always change your situation quickly.The quote has lasted because it lets people ignore what's expected of them and work out for themselves what a fulfilling life looks like.The deeper lesson behind Princess Diana's quoteDiana's words make us question whether love really is the final answer to being happy. Relationships bring warmth and a sense of belonging, but they can't replace self-respect, your own interests or a sense of purpose.A job you find fulfilling lets you use your talents and be part of something that matters, and over time you see your hard work pay off. Other people find the same feeling through studying, caring for family members, volunteering or creative work.In the end, what matters most is that your life feels worthwhile to you, and not only to the people watching or because you have a partner.So the lesson to take from this quote is that a relationship can make your life better, but it doesn't have to define who you are. Your work and your own ambitions can give you independence and confidence, and a reason to keep going. The most fulfilling life is one that matches your values and has room for the people you love as well as for your own growth.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: FBI's Winter SHIELD and Riptide: Kash Patel says 750 companies contacted, 200 cybercriminals arrested as US steps up cyber defence
articles.summary: The FBI has engaged more than 750 private-sector companies and arrested over 200 cybercriminals as part of two separate campaigns aimed at protecting
articles.body: The FBI has engaged more than 750 private-sector companies and arrested over 200 cybercriminals as part of two separate campaigns aimed at protecting American businesses and critical infrastructure from cyberattacks, FBI Director Kash Patel said during a television appearance on Thursday. Speaking to Fox News host Sean Hannity on November 19, Patel discussed the bureau's Operation Winter SHIELD and Operation Riptide, explaining how the two initiatives were designed to tackle different aspects of the growing cybersecurity threat.While Winter SHIELD focuses on strengthening the digital defences of businesses, government agencies and critical infrastructure, Riptide targets cybercriminals through arrests, extraditions, financial seizures and disruption of their technical infrastructure.Patel's remarks came amid concerns over a series of technology disruptions affecting banks, airlines, email networks and federal agencies in the US. He said intelligence assessments had found no evidence that foreign adversaries or outside groups were responsible for the reported outages. Patel attributed the disruptions to the rapid replacement of outdated technology and legacy software systems by government agencies and private companies."There are going to be some technical disruptions like we've seen, but the FBI and the intelligence community is going to continuously monitor those activities for nefarious actors," Patel said.He added that the FBI would hunt down anyone found responsible for malicious cyber activity.What is Operation Winter SHIELD?Operation Winter SHIELD, which stands for Securing Homeland Infrastructure by Enhancing Layered Defense, is an FBI cybersecurity initiative designed to help organisations strengthen their protection against hackers and other malicious actors. The bureau launched the 60-day campaign in 2026, bringing together its field offices, private-sector partners and government agencies to improve the security of critical infrastructure.According to Patel, FBI teams have met with more than 750 private-sector companies to establish direct communication channels and encourage businesses to cooperate with federal investigators when cyber intrusions occur.In September testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee, Patel said all 56 FBI field offices had participated in the campaign, conducting more than 600 engagements across 14 critical infrastructure sectors.The initiative focuses on improving cybersecurity practices, identifying vulnerabilities and ensuring that businesses can respond quickly when their systems are compromised.The FBI has also encouraged companies to adopt 10 defensive measures, including stronger authentication systems, vulnerability management, secure backups, restricted administrator access and regular testing of incident response plans.Patel compares cyberattacks to hostage situationsDuring his Fox News appearance, Patel stressed that the first 24 to 48 hours after a cyber intrusion are particularly important. He compared the initial response to a cyberattack to dealing with a hostage situation, saying investigators need immediate access to affected systems to identify attackers and contain the damage.Patel cited an incident last year in which hackers targeted several banks on a Friday afternoon.According to him, the banks quickly cooperated with the FBI, allowing cyber teams to access their systems and remove the attackers by Sunday before any money or customer information was stolen. He said the bureau wanted companies to involve federal investigators early rather than wait until an attack had caused substantial damage.Private companies are not automatically required to give the FBI access to their networks. The initiative therefore relies on voluntary cooperation between businesses and federal authorities.Operation Riptide: FBI arrests more than 200 cybercriminalsWhile Winter SHIELD is focused on preventing cyberattacks, Operation Riptide represents the FBI's offensive approach to tackling cybercrime.The bureau conducted Riptide as a separate 60-day international law enforcement campaign targeting cybercriminal networks that steal money, compromise computer systems and exploit American individuals and businesses.According to Patel, the operation involved 13 coordinated actions with US and international law enforcement partners.In an earlier video outlining the results, the FBI director said the campaign resulted in more than 200 arrests and the freezing or seizure of over $23 million in illicit cryptocurrency and other funds.The FBI also initiated the return of another $31 million in virtual assets stolen by North Korean cybercriminals. Patel said the operation demonstrated how coordinated investigations, financial tracking and international cooperation could disrupt criminal networks operating across borders.He added that cybercriminals could no longer assume that they could escape American law enforcement simply by operating from another country."Operation Riptide may be over, but we aren't anywhere close to done," Patel said in a video released by the FBI. The bureau said its commitment to disrupting cyber threats and pursuing criminals would continue beyond the 60-day campaign.Patel says FBI has arrested 200 cybercriminals under Trump administrationDuring his November 19 interview, Patel also highlighted the broader action taken against cybercriminals since the Trump administration took office. He said the FBI had arrested 200 cybercriminals during the administration, including six suspects extradited from overseas.Patel also referred to Operation Blackout, a separate anti-fraud initiative under which federal authorities have seized $17 billion in foreign assets, according to his remarks.FBI warns Americans about phishing and online scamsPatel said protecting America's digital infrastructure was not solely the responsibility of federal agencies and large corporations. He urged ordinary Americans to remain alert to phishing attempts, suspicious emails and online scams that could expose personal information or compromise financial accounts. The FBI has encouraged individuals and businesses to report suspicious activity and use its official cybersecurity resources.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Meet Jaz Stewart, the 19-year-old who travelled 4,000 km for a cattle station job in Australia after Covid cancelled her Canada plans; a six-month job turned into a new life among 42,000 cattle and an orphaned camel
articles.summary: At 19, Jaz Stewart was expecting to spend her gap year travelling overseas before going to university.
articles.body: At 19, Jaz Stewart was expecting to spend her gap year travelling overseas before going to university. Canada was the plan, with the prospect of a year or two away from home. Instead, the pandemic changed her plans and sent her in a very different direction. She travelled thousands of kilometres from Moree in New South Wales to Flora Valley Station in Western Australia's Kimberley region, taking up a job in the kitchen of a cattle property, as reported by the National Farmers' Federation. What began as an alternative to overseas travel gradually turned into something longer term. She found herself learning the routines of station life, working around cattle and caring for an orphaned camel, while developing a photography career alongside her work.How a 19-year-old landed a cooking job at a remote Australian cattle stationBefore arriving in Western Australia, Stewart had spent two years working at a café in Moree after finishing school. She had grown up around the agricultural industry through her family's earthmoving contracting business, but had not been raised on a farm. Her schooling, meanwhile, had taken her to a boarding school in Sydney.The original intention was to travel to Canada and eventually return to Australia for university. Covid disrupted those arrangements, leaving her to consider other ways of spending the time before further study. In 2021, she accepted a position at Flora Valley Station, roughly 4,000 kilometres from her hometown, as reported by the National Farmers' Federation.The job was initially meant to last six months. Stewart arrived as a station cook, with little indication that the move would alter her plans for work and study. The property was about two hours from Halls Creek, one of the nearest small towns, and the distance from familiar surroundings was considerable.Daily routine of a remote 42,000-head cattle stationCooking was Stewart's original responsibility, but her curiosity about the work happening outside the homestead soon took her elsewhere on the property. She began spending time watching the station's workers manage cattle, taking her camera along as she became familiar with the daily activities.It did not take long for observation to turn into participation. Having watched the work being carried out, she gradually picked up the practical skills and was given tasks of her own. The station operated on a substantial scale, running approximately 42,000 cattle, and offered a working environment quite different from the café where she had previously been employed.The change was not simply about learning another job. Stewart was getting an introduction to the demands of remote agricultural work, where days could involve physical tasks, unexpected problems and long stretches away from town. Her initial six-month commitment also began to look less realistic as she settled into the routine.How an orphaned camel became part of station lifeAmong the animals Stewart encountered at Flora Valley was Calli, a young camel whose arrival had been anything but planned. The animal had been separated from her mother and left without care following a bushfire. Stewart's manager came across her while away on a stock camp and began feeding and looking after her.Keeping the camel at that location was not possible under the company's policies, so she was transported to the Flora Valley homestead in the back of a minivan. Stewart took responsibility for bottle-feeding her over the following months.Calli spent much of her early time alongside the station's poddy calves, young animals being raised by people rather than their mothers. As she grew, she was moved into a paddock with them. Her early behaviour had been difficult to miss, with loud calls that irritated some of the station workers. Eventually, she became more settled and comfortable among the other animals.Stewart developed a close bond with her. Calli would recognise her when she entered the paddock and come over when called, often looking for attention and scratches. There were some adjustments to make, too. The property had plenty of horses, and their initial reaction to having a camel around was less than welcoming. The animals gradually became accustomed to one another.Photography became another part of her working lifeThe Kimberley landscape also gave Stewart an opportunity to develop an interest that had started alongside her station duties. She regularly photographed the country around her, from its distinctive red and brown landscapes to the people and animals that made up everyday life on the property.What began as taking pictures while observing cattle work developed into something more serious. She started building her photography skills and eventually took on professional work, documenting the people, scenery and quieter moments of station life.Her photographs also offered glimpses of what happened away from the day's agricultural responsibilities. The people working on remote properties often had their own ways of spending their limited time off, and Stewart's images captured some of these everyday details.University plans began to look differentBefore moving west, Stewart had considered studying primary education at university. By the time she spoke about her experience in September 2022, however, she was no longer certain that this was the direction she wanted to take.Living in the Kimberley had introduced her to opportunities she had not considered while growing up. Agriculture was now a possible career, while tourism was another area she was interested in exploring. She had also developed professional and personal connections in different parts of Australia through her work.That did not mean the transition had been entirely straightforward. Living around two hours from Halls Creek brought a degree of isolation, and the distance from family and familiar surroundings could be difficult. The climate was another adjustment. Stewart mentioned enjoying temperatures of around 25 to 30 degrees Celsius while her family back home in New South Wales were experiencing much colder conditions.By then, she had moved well beyond the six months she originally intended to spend at the station. The possibility of staying in the Kimberley for longer had become part of her plans, although travelling elsewhere remained an interest.A life she had not expected to chooseStewart's experience was a departure from the future she had imagined at school. She had not planned to settle in the Kimberley, much less build a working life around a remote cattle property. Yet the combination of practical experience, photography and the relationships she formed there had changed how she viewed her options.She also encouraged other young people to consider spending time in the Australian outback, even if they were unsure whether it would suit them long term. Station work, as she described it, could mean learning unfamiliar tasks, dealing with problems and getting through demanding days.For Stewart, the social side of the experience mattered as much as the work itself. Shared evening meals and conversations with fellow station workers had become part of the routine. A move originally made because an overseas trip was no longer possible had introduced her to a different career direction, a new home and an unlikely companion in Calli the camel.You use AI every day. Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving, and this year, it falls on Friday, Nov. 27. That said, many retailers kick off their Black Friday sales earlier, which is why this month is often referred to as "Black November." Yes, this means you'll be bombarded with holiday sale messaging long before your turkey has even defrosted, but the good news is, you'll be able to get a head start on your gift shopping ahead of the Black Friday hubbub.

What is the difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday?

Black Friday sales usually continue through the holiday weekend and into Cyber Monday, which is on Monday, Nov. 30. While the two savings events have merged into one long weekend of markdowns for the most part, Black Friday sales often involve a mix of in-store and online discounts, whereas Cyber Monday has historically been a web-focused sale extravaganza.

Deals will vary from retailer to retailer, so just because you see something on sale during Black Friday, don't assume it'll still be discounted for Cyber Monday. When in doubt, add to cart and check out!

During sales like Prime Day , we usually advise readers to hold off on purchasing items in the tech and large appliance categories — and that's because it's worth waiting until Black Friday. If you've wanted to upgrade your TV or get a new dishwasher, this is the time to do it!

To be honest, there's not much we wouldn't recommend buying during Black Friday; most major retailers will be offering some of their deepest discounts of the year on everything from kitchen essentials to beauty favorites, and it's also a stellar time to stock up on clothing. Of course, many of us will be shopping for gifts, so if you see something on your list for a great price, grab it before it sells out.

The only things you should steer clear of? Bad deals. Not all Black Friday sales are created equal, so it's important to pick out the legit markdowns from the duds. Retailers can sneakily raise starting prices to make a discount seem more impressive than it is, and it's always a good idea to compare sales across the web to make sure you're getting the best price. (Actually, that's our job, and you can think of this as your one-stop shop for all things Black Friday this month.)

articles.title: A US dairy farm turned manure from 11,000 cows into renewable fuel for its milk trucks, producing 865 million BTUs of gas daily and saving more than 1.5 million gallons of diesel every year
articles.summary: Fair Oaks Farms produced more than milk from its herd of 11,000 dairy cows.
articles.body: Fair Oaks Farms produced more than milk from its herd of 11,000 dairy cows. Its anaerobic digester processed waste from the dairy operation and generated approximately 865 million British thermal units (BTUs) of renewable natural gas each day. The main waste product used in the project was animal manure.According to the US Department of Agriculture (USDA), the gas produced by the digester was converted into renewable compressed natural gas (CNG). This gave the farm a source of transportation fuel made from waste generated by its own dairy operations. The digester generated this renewable natural gas as part of the farm’s waste-to-energy project.How did Fair Oaks Farms turn cow manure into fuel for its trucksFair Oaks Farms used waste from its herd of 11,000 dairy cows to produce renewable fuel alongside milk. Its anaerobic digester broke down waste from the dairy operation, mainly cow manure, to generate around 865 million British thermal units (BTUs) of renewable natural gas every day as of 2019. The gas was then processed into renewable compressed natural gas (CNG), which could be used as vehicle fuel.This allowed the farm to turn manure produced by its own dairy operations into a source of energy for transportation. The waste-to-energy project also helped meet the fuel requirements of the farm’s milk transport trucks, which carried milk to processing plants. It connected the farm's waste management system with its transportation needs.What equipment helped turn dairy waste into vehicle fuelThe project required machinery and equipment to turn methane gas from the dairy’s digester into renewable compressed natural gas. The equipment removed carbon dioxide from the biogas, so it could be used as a transportation fuel. A fueling station was also installed as part of the work.It had facilities for gas drying, compressing, and dispensing. These steps prepared the gas for use by the farm’s trucks. articles.title: Rob Reiner and Michele Reiner’s daughter Romy Reiner sells Los Angeles home for $10.3 million in all-cash deal months after parents’ murder; inside the Brentwood property once owned by Norman Lear
articles.summary: Romy Reiner, the daughter of late filmmaker Rob Reiner and his wife Michele Reiner, has sold the Los Angeles property where she was living when her
articles.body: Romy Reiner, the daughter of late filmmaker Rob Reiner and his wife Michele Reiner, has sold the Los Angeles property where she was living when her parents were murdered at their nearby Brentwood home last year. According to real estate records obtained by PEOPLE, the property was sold for $10.3 million in an all-cash deal on February 17, 2026.The Brentwood property was purchased by a limited liability company (LLC) through a trust associated with the Reiner family. It has also been linked to other real estate holdings owned by the family in California.The property had a long history in Hollywood. Rob and Michele purchased the Brentwood home in 1991 from television producer Norman Lear, according to the Los Angeles Times. The couple lived there for decades.The approximately 10,000-square-foot, two-storey New England-style house featured six bedrooms, six bathrooms and two staff quarters. The property also had a swimming pool, a pool pavilion, gardens and a tennis court on a separate lot across the street.Before Lear, the home had belonged to Oscar-winning actor Henry Fonda, who owned it after it was built in 1936. It was later sold to actor Paul Henreid, known for his role in Casablanca. Lear had owned the property since 1972.Rob once spoke about his connection to the house during a February 2015 appearance on PBS. He recalled visiting the property to play tennis when he was working on All in the Family and telling himself that it was the kind of home he would like to own someday."I would go over there and I used to say, 'Boy, if ever I get money, if ever I have some money to buy a house, this is the kind of house that I would like,'" he said, describing its appeal as its "New England charm".When he and Michele were looking for a home after getting married, she came across the property without initially realising its connection to Lear. Rob recalled that she noticed several pictures of Lear inside and wondered whether the owners were particularly fond of him. He then explained that it was Lear's home and that it was exactly the kind of house he had always wanted.Reiner home was also a gathering place for political figuresBeyond its place in the filmmaker's personal life, the Brentwood property was also known for hosting political gatherings. Rob said Lear had organised several political events there before selling the house to the couple.During the PBS appearance, Rob recalled that when he proposed an addition to the property to the Brentwood Park Association, members asked whether he planned to host a lot of political events there.He joked that the couple ended up doing the opposite of what they had been asked to avoid. Rob also revealed that former US President Bill Clinton, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and former Vice President Al Gore had visited the house."A lot of political things have floated through that house," he said.Romy was living across the street when parents were murderedRomy, 28, was reportedly living across the street from her parents at the time of their deaths. She was the first to discover her father's body inside the Brentwood home on December 14, 2025, PEOPLE previously reported.According to The New York Times, her brother Jake, 35, lived about a mile away, while their brother Nick, 33, was staying in their parents' guesthouse.Soon after Rob and Michele were found dead, Nick was arrested and charged with two counts of first-degree murder in connection with their deaths. Rob was 78 and Michele was 70.Nick is currently being held without bail at the Twin Towers Correctional Facility in Los Angeles. In August 2026, he was indicted on both charges and pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he could face life imprisonment without the possibility of parole or the death penalty. The criminal case remains pending.Romy and Jake Reiner honour parents at public eventAlmost a year after their parents' deaths, Romy and Jake made a rare public appearance together at the Children's Institute's Cape & Gown Gala in Los Angeles on November 8. The siblings were there to honour their parents' legacy of activism and present the inaugural Michele and Rob Reiner Champion for Change Award to their longtime family friend, actor Jamie Lee Curtis.While presenting the award at the Beverly Wilshire hotel, Jake spoke about the values his parents stood for and their efforts to make a difference in the lives of children."I love the name for this award: Champion for Change. That's what our parents stood for. They were never satisfied with the status quo; they were always champions for change to make the world better," Jake said.He also spoke about how their commitment to children began within their own family. "The work my parents did for children started at home, creating a loving environment for us from the moment I was born and long after Romy was born," he added.Romy also praised Curtis for the support she had given the family during a difficult period."Jamie is someone who believes in the good in people, and will do everything in her power to make a situation right. She will move mountains not just because she can, but because she feels that it is the right thing to do. Her love and generosity during this time have meant more to me than she'll ever know," she said.Curtis joined the siblings on stage to accept the award and remembered the couple, saying, "Rob and Michele lived so fiercely, so loudly."Rob Reiner's celebrated career in HollywoodRob Reiner built a celebrated career in Hollywood as an actor and filmmaker. He directed several acclaimed films, including This Is Spinal Tap (1984), Stand by Me (1986) and When Harry Met Sally... (1989). He first became widely known for playing Mike Stivic in Norman Lear's sitcom All in the Family.Lear and Reiner remained close long after the show ended in the late 1970s. Their association eventually led to Reiner and Michele purchasing Lear's Brentwood home in 1991, where they lived for decades.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: A Brooklyn Heights apartment once rented by Ed Sheeran has been listed for $12.5 million. The British singer paid $36,000 a month for the waterfront residence in 2023, when it was the borough’s most expensive lease of the year. The four-bedroom property is part of the Pierhouse condominium development and overlooks Brooklyn Bridge Park. It spans 3,239 square feet across several levels and includes private balconies and a rooftop terrace.According to the New York Post, the home also offers views of the Manhattan skyline, the East River, and the Statue of Liberty. Sheeran later bought a different apartment in the same waterfront development with his wife, Cherry Seaborn, in May 2025.Ed Sheeran’s former Brooklyn rental is now listed for $12.5 millionThe residence is located in Pierhouse, a waterfront condominium development in Brooklyn Heights. It covers 3,239 square feet and is arranged across multiple levels. The four-bedroom home has private balconies and a rooftop terrace, as well as views across the water towards Manhattan, the East River, and the Statue of Liberty.The property is positioned beside Brooklyn Bridge Park. Its current asking price is $12.5 million. The apartment last changed hands in 2018, when it sold for slightly more than $6 million.That means the present asking price is more than twice the amount paid by its previous buyer. The listing is represented by Sarah Williams and Peter Stack of Societe Real Estate.Ed Sheeran’s former rental attracted a professional athlete at $38,000 a monthSheeran rented the Brooklyn Heights apartment in 2023 for $36,000 a month. The New York Post reported that the lease made it the most expensive rental in the borough that year. The singer first moved into the property during a period when he was also facing a copyright infringement trial in Manhattan over his song ‘Thinking Out Loud’. A jury ultimately ruled in his favour.Sheeran’s stay at the residence did not mark the end of his connection with the development. After leaving the apartment, he went on to buy another home in the same waterfront development with his wife, Cherry Seaborn.After Sheeran moved out, the apartment was offered for rent again in 2024, this time at $38,000 a month. The property was later rented to a professional athlete. The asking rent was $2,000 more per month than what Sheeran had paid.The apartment has since returned to the property market, but this time as a sale rather than a rental. The purchase was made through an off-market deal involving a UK-registered entity linked to the couple.The couple bought their own home in the development after spending two years living there as renters. articles.title: Florida couple take their dog for a late-night walk and discover a 15-foot, 134-pound Burmese python hiding in a neighbour's bushes; a local trapper captures the invasive snake in just three minutes
articles.summary: An ordinary late-night dog walk turned into an extraordinary wildlife encounter for a Florida couple after they stumbled upon one of the largest snakes
articles.body: An ordinary late-night dog walk turned into an extraordinary wildlife encounter for a Florida couple after they stumbled upon one of the largest snakes they had ever seen hiding in a neighbour's bushes. What initially began as a neighbourhood warning about a possible snake sighting quickly developed into a gathering of curious residents and an urgent call for professional assistance. By the time a local trapper arrived, the creature had been identified as a massive Burmese python measuring more than 15 feet and weighing 134 pounds.Neighbour's warning leads to unexpected discoveryAccording to Naples News Now and AOL, the incident took place on November 6 in Chase Preserve, a residential community within Lely Resort, southeast of Naples, Florida.Kristen Bowerman first learned about the snake when a neighbour spotted it near a sidewalk on Celeste Drive while walking with her husband. The resident filmed the massive reptile and sent it to Bowerman, who shared it on the community's group messaging app. t 10 p.m., Bowerman and her husband, Scott, took their dog for its last walk.However, their routine outing quickly took an unexpected turn when they noticed several neighbours gathered near some bushes. Residents had located the snake hiding in the landscaping close to a nearby home.According to AOL, Scott approached the area to get a closer look and recorded the encounter, while Kristen kept their dog at a safe distance.Professional trapper captures 134-pound pythonWith a potentially dangerous invasive snake hiding close to residential properties, professional assistance was sought.Naples News Now reported that Kenne Helm, a local wildlife trapper operating as Trapper Helm, responded to the sighting.Despite the python's enormous size, Helm managed to capture it in approximately three minutes after entering the bushes where it had been hiding.Following its capture, the snake was measured and weighed. It turned out to be a female Burmese python measuring 15 feet and two inches long and weighing 134 pounds.According to AOL, Helm believed the snake was moving through the area during the seasonal reproductive period, potentially searching for a mate before nesting. The python was subsequently humanely euthanized, and its remains were handed over to a python biologist for research, as reported by both publications.Why Burmese pythons are a concern in FloridaThe discovery highlights the continuing challenges Florida faces because of its growing invasive Burmese python population.According to Naples News Now, these large constrictors are not native to the United States and originally come from parts of Asia. In Florida, they are mostly associated with captive animals that escaped or were released and reproduced in the wild.The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) identifies Burmese pythons as an established invasive species across significant parts of South Florida.AOL reported that their established range stretches from south of Lake Okeechobee to Key Largo, extending westward through parts of Broward County into Collier County.Although Burmese pythons can grow beyond 20 feet, those captured in Florida generally measure between six and 10 feet. The Chase Preserve specimen was therefore considerably larger than the typical captured adult.Invasive snakes threaten native wildlife and petsBurmese pythons are powerful non-venomous constrictors that prey on mammals, birds and reptiles. Their presence can put pressure on native wildlife populations and disrupt the ecological balance of South Florida.Their size and strength can also make them a potential danger to household pets, particularly smaller dogs and cats.According to Naples News Now, Helm's company participates in a volunteer response programme that helps Collier County residents remove large invasive constrictors without charging them for the service.Residents urged to avoid approaching large snakesThe unusual encounter serves as a reminder that residents should exercise caution when spotting large snakes around their homes.Naples News Now reported that people should avoid attempting to capture or handle Burmese pythons themselves.Image Courtesy: AOLYou use AI every day. articles.title: Quote of the day by Michael Jackson: "You never know how long you have with someone, so don't forget to say…"
articles.summary: Life doesn't send a warning before it changes. The people we see every day, at home, at work or on the other end of a phone call, may not always be around.
articles.body: Life doesn't send a warning before it changes. The people we see every day, at home, at work or on the other end of a phone call, may not always be around. Moments that feel very normal right now can turn into memories we hold on to for years. Michael Jackson's quote talks about this uncertainty in a simple way. Don't assume you'll always get another chance to tell someone you love them.This isn't only about couples. It's about your parents and children, your brothers and sisters, your friends, and really anyone who makes your life better by being in it. A quick phone call or a warm message may not seem like much when you send it, but for the person on the other side it can mean a lot.The quote also pushes us past the awkwardness many of us feel about showing emotion. A lot of people save their feelings for birthdays and anniversaries, or they just assume their loved ones already know. Some feelings shouldn't stay unsaid for that long. Often the words that stay with someone are the ones you said on a completely normal Tuesday.Quote of the day by Michael Jackson"You never know how long you have with someone, so don't forget to say I love you while you can"What is the meaning of Michael Jackson's quoteThe main idea is that you should tell people you love them while you still can, because nobody knows how much time they'll get with the people they care about.Most of us keep putting these conversations off. We'll call Mummy later. We'll tell a friend how much they've helped us when the right moment comes. We'll say something sweet to our partner once things calm down at work. But life is unpredictable, and those moments aren't promised to anyone.When he says "you never know how long you have with someone", he's reminding us that a lot of things can affect our relationships and we can't control most of them. People move to another city. Someone falls ill. Life gets busy, years go by, and we end up seeing the people we love far less than we used to.The second half, "don't forget to say I love you while you can", turns that thought into something you can actually do. Don't sit around waiting for the perfect moment. Say what you feel today.The point isn't to be scared of losing people. It's to notice how much they matter while they're still here with you.Why expressing love should not be postponedWe often think our loved ones already know how much we value them. And yes, they can probably see it in what we do. Even so, actually hearing the words gives people comfort and reassurance in a way that actions sometimes can't.A parent might be quietly happy to hear that all their hard work made a difference. A friend might need to know you noticed how they stood by you, and your partner might just like being reminded that they're loved.You don't need fancy words or a big surprise for any of this. One honest sentence can say what months of routine conversations didn't.Putting it off can also slowly push people apart. When everyone is busy with work and responsibilities, conversations become practical. Who's picking up the groceries, when the bill is due, what time the meeting is. Love is assumed and rarely spoken.Jackson's words ask us to make space for honest feelings even when nothing special is going on.Why the people closest to us can be taken for grantedWhen someone is always around, it's easy to feel they always will be.We get used to Papa's daily call, a friend's good-morning texts, a partner being there when we come home, or simply knowing someone will pick up when we need them. Because it happens every day, we stop noticing how precious it is.It's usually not that we care less. Routine just makes love harder to see.Someone can love their family deeply and still go weeks without saying so. Two friends can share years of memories and never once talk about what the friendship means to them. A married couple can get so caught up in running the house that they forget to thank each other.The quote is a reminder that being close to someone is no excuse for being careless about showing them they matter.Love is expressed through actions as well as wordsThe quote talks about saying "I love you", but what it means goes further than those three words.You also show love when you pay attention to someone, when you're kind and patient, and when people know they can count on you. It's there when you check on someone who's unwell, when you listen without cutting them off, when you remember their important day, or when you make time for a person who's going through something hard.Words matter, and they matter more when your actions match them.Telling your mother you love her is important. Calling her regularly, helping when she needs it and actually listening to what's worrying her is what makes that love real for her.Friendships work the same way. Saying a friend matters is good, but turning up when life gets tough is what makes the friendship stronger.What we can learn from this is to make love a part of everyday life, so it isn't kept only for special days.Why saying "I love you" can feel difficultIt's a short sentence, but it isn't always easy to say.Many of us grew up in homes where feelings simply weren't talked about. Some people find it uncomfortable to be that open, or they worry the other person won't understand. Bad experiences in the past can make people careful about showing their feelings too.In some relationships, love shows up more in what people do than in what they say. A father may show it by working long hours for his family. A friend may show it by always being the first to help.These ways of caring are real and they deserve to be noticed. Still, they don't make the words unnecessary.Saying something loving, honestly and in a way that suits the relationship, can bring two people closer.You don't have to wait until emotions are overflowing or something goes wrong. Small, honest words now and then can make conversations warmer and easier.Why time with loved ones is more valuable than we realiseOnce time has passed, you can't get it back.People often remember the simple moments more clearly than expensive gifts or big parties. A meal together, chai and a long chat late at night, an old joke only the two of you get, or a short evening walk with someone close can end up as a memory you treasure.We don't always see how special these moments are while they're happening. It usually hits us later, when routines change or someone moves away.Jackson's quote asks us to pay attention to now, instead of assuming we can always recreate these moments later.That doesn't mean dropping your responsibilities or spending every minute with family. It means making a real effort to stay in touch, however busy you are.A short call, a thoughtful message or a conversation where nobody's rushing can keep a relationship from slowly fading.How to apply Michael Jackson's quote in everyday lifeYou can put this message into practice with a few small habits.Say what you feel: Don't assume people know how much they mean to you. Tell them honestly when you appreciate or love them.Make time for family: Call or visit your parents, siblings and relatives when you can. You don't need to wait for Diwali, Eid, Christmas or a wedding to do it.Appreciate your friends: Tell your friends when their support or kindness, or just having them around, has made a difference to you.Avoid unnecessary postponement: If you've been meaning to get back in touch with someone, make the first move when the time feels right.Listen carefully: Giving someone your full attention, phone down, is another way of showing them they matter.Resolve misunderstandings: Where you can, talk things out honestly so small hurts don't grow into bigger ones.Show affection through actions: Help, encourage and support the people you love, and do it consistently, not only in words.None of this needs a special date or a perfect setting. What makes it count is that you mean it.Why the quote is relevant in the age of constant communicationIt has never been easier to reach people. A message can cross the world in seconds, video calls bring faraway families into the same room, and social media lets friends keep up with each other's lives even when they're busy.But having more ways to talk doesn't mean we talk about what matters.Someone can send dozens of messages a day and never really have a conversation. A family can be scattered across cities, all in the same WhatsApp group, sharing good-morning images, and still not find time for one proper phone call.Texts and calls can keep a relationship going, but they can't replace real attention and honesty, which is what gives a relationship its meaning.So the quote reminds us to use all these tools for more than just passing on information. We can use them to say thank you, to say we care, and to make someone feel reassured.The difference between loving someone and making them feel lovedYou can care about someone very deeply and still not show it well.A person may assume their partner knows they're appreciated. A son or daughter may believe their parents already know how grateful they are. One friend may expect another to understand how much their support meant.Relationships grow stronger when love isn't left for the other person to guess.Making someone feel loved means understanding what matters to them. For one person it might be encouragement, and for another it's time spent together. It could be remembering small details, respecting how they feel, or just telling them they're important to you.The quote nudges us to close the gap between what we feel inside and what the people around us actually get to experience.The deeper lesson behind Michael Jackson's quoteAt its core, this quote is about seeing the value of people before life forces us to.It asks us not to treat love as something we can always express later. We can make all the plans we want, but none of us knows how much time we'll get with the people who matter.That doesn't mean worrying every time you say goodbye, or measuring a relationship by how often you say "I love you". It means being a bit more deliberate about showing that you care.Strong relationships are built out of everyday moments. The conversations we make time for, the help we offer, the arguments we try to fix and the love we show without needing a reason.So here's what to take away. Don't make the people you love guess how much they mean to you. Tell them and show them, and make time for them while you can. Something loving you say today may turn out to be one of the most meaningful things you ever give them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: First regular India-Nepal passenger train to link birthplaces of Lord Ram and Mata Sita
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: After a gap over two years, Indian railways will run a direct cross-border passenger train.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: After a gap over two years, Indian railways will run a direct cross-border passenger train. This time to Nepal, to link Lord Ram’s birthplace Ayodhya to that of Mata Sita’s in Janakpur. The move will not only connect the two cities revered by Hindus, promoting religious tourism, but also play the larger role of strengthening bilateral relations.TOI has learnt that PM Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah will virtually flag off the train on its inaugural run on Nov 23 (Sunday). As per a railway ministry notification, the weekly train from Janakpur will depart every Saturday afternoon while departure from Ayodhya will be every Monday afternoon.The last cross-border trains that India operated were Maitree and Bandhan Express to Bangladesh. The services were suspended indefinitely in July-Aug 2024 following violent protests and political turmoil in the neighbouring nation. There is no sign of the operation resuming anytime soon.Earlier, India’s passenger train services to Pakistan — Samjhauta Express and Thar Express — were suspended in Aug 2019 after govt revoked J&K’s special status under Article 320 and the subsequent deterioration in bilateral relations.So, the direct train to Janakpur will be the only active cross-border link from India in the region.“This will be the first direct passenger train from India to Nepal. At present, passengers from India can travel up to Jaynagar station in Bihar by Indian Railways, then they need to undergo customs clearance and board trains run by Nepal Railways to reach Janakpur Dham and Kurtha in Nepal. However, in the case of Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham train, passengers will continue to travel in the same train after customs clearance,” said an official.The one-way journey of around 604 km will take approximately 19 hours. The train with AC2, AC3 and sleeper coaches can accommodate around 1,100 passengers. The train will stop at stations including Mankapur, Basti, Gorakhpur, Narkatiaganj, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Shisho, Madhubani and Jaynagar.
